title: Pre-computed memory or on-the-fly encoding? A hybrid approach to retrieval augmentation makes the most of your compute
creator: Michiel de Jong, Yury Zemlyanskiy, Nicholas FitzGerald, Joshua Ainslie, Sumit Sanghai, Fei Sha, William W. Cohen
description: Abstract Retrieval-augmented language models such as Fusion-in-Decoder are powerful, setting the state of the art on a variety of knowledge-intensive tasks. However, they are also expensive, due to the need to encode a large number of retrieved passages. Some work avoids this cost by pre-encoding a text corpus into a memory and retrieving dense representations directly.

title: On extremal problems on multigraphs
creator: Ran Gu, Shuaichao Wang
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ran Gu, Shuaichao Wang. An ( n , s , q ) (n,s,q) -graph is an n n -vertex multigraph in which every s s -set of vertices spans at most q q edges. Erdős initiated the study of maximum number of edges of ( n , s , q ) (n,s,q) -graphs, and the extremal problem on multigraphs has been considered since the 1990s.

title: An equivariant generalisation of McDuff–Segal’s group–completion theorem Thanks: Date of publication in IMRN .
creator: Kaif Hilman
description: Abstract In this short note, we prove a G G –equivariant generalisation of McDuff–Segal’s group–completion theorem for finite groups G G . A new complication regarding genuine equivariant localisations arises and we resolve this by isolating a simple condition on the homotopy groups of 𝔼 ∞ \mathbb{E}_{\infty} –rings in G G –spectra.

title: Black hole perturbations in Maxwell-Horndeski theories
creator: Ryotaro Kase 1 and Shinji Tsujikawa 2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ryotaro Kase 1 and Shinji Tsujikawa 2. We study the linear stability of black holes in Maxwell-Horndeski theories where a U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge-invariant vector field is coupled to a scalar field with the Lagrangian of full Horndeski theories. The perturbations on a static and spherically symmetric background can be decomposed into odd- and even-parity modes under the expansion of spherical harmonics with multipoles l l .

title: High-Throughput Rate-Flexible Combinational Decoders for Multi-Kernel Polar Codes PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2023 IEEE
creator: Hossein Rezaei, Nandana Rajatheva, Matti Latva-aho
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hossein Rezaei, Nandana Rajatheva, Matti Latva-aho. Polar codes have received growing attention in the past decade and have been selected as the coding scheme for the control channel in the fifth generation (5G) wireless communication systems. However, the conventional polar codes have only been constructed by binary ( 2 × 2 2\times 2 ) kernel which poses block length limitation to powers of 2 2 . To attain more flexible block lengths, multi-kernel polar codes are proposed.

title: HAL3D: Hierarchical Active Learning for Fine-Grained 3D Part Labeling
creator: Fenggen Yu, Yiming Qian, Francisca Gil-Ureta, Brian Jackson, Eric Bennett, Hao Zhang
description: Abstract We present the first active learning tool for fine-grained 3D part labeling, a problem which challenges even the most advanced deep learning (DL) methods due to the significant structural variations among the intricate parts. For the same reason, the necessary effort to annotate training data is tremendous, motivating approaches to minimize human involvement.

title: On algebraic and non-algebraic neighborhoods of rational curves Thanks: This study was partially supported by the HSE University Basic Research Program and by SRISA research project FNEF-2022-0007 (Reg. No 1021060909180-7-1.2.1).
creator: Serge Lvovski
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Serge Lvovski. We prove that for any d > 0 d>0 there exists an embedding of the Riemann sphere ℙ 1 \mathbb{P}^{1} in a smooth complex surface, with self-intersection d d , such that the germ of this embedding cannot be extended to an embedding in an algebraic surface but the field of germs of meromorphic functions along C C has transcendence degree 2 2 over ℂ \mathbb{C} .

title: Scaling the tail beat frequency and swimming speed in underwater undulatory swimming
creator: Jesús Sánchez-Rodríguez, Christophe Raufaste, Médéric Argentina
description: Abstract Due to its great efficiency and maneuverability, undulatory swimming is the predominant form of locomotion in aquatic vertebrates. A myriad of animals of different species and sizes oscillate their bodies to propel themselves in aquatic environments with swimming speed scaling as the product of the animal length by the oscillation frequency.

title: On the rainbow planar Turán number of paths
creator: Ervin Győri, Ryan R. Martin, Addisu Paulos, Casey Tompkins, Kitti Varga
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ervin Győri, Ryan R. Martin, Addisu Paulos, Casey Tompkins, Kitti Varga. An edge-colored graph is said to contain a rainbow- F F if it contains F F as a subgraph and every edge of F F is a distinct color. The problem of maximizing edges among n n -vertex properly edge-colored graphs not containing a rainbow- F F , known as the rainbow Turán problem, was initiated by Keevash, Mubayi, Sudakov and Verstraëte.

title: XLM-V: Overcoming the Vocabulary Bottleneck in Multilingual Masked Language Models
creator: Davis Liang, Hila Gonen, Yuning Mao, Rui Hou, Marjan Ghazvininejad, Luke Zettlemoyer, Madian Khabsa
description: Abstract Large multilingual language models typically rely on a single vocabulary shared across 100+ languages. As these models have increased in parameter count and depth, vocabulary size has remained largely unchanged. This vocabulary bottleneck limits the representational capabilities of multilingual models like XLM-R.

title: Mapping the X-ray variability of GRS 1915+105 with machine learning 2022 Mapping the X-ray variability of GRS 1915+105 with machine learning – B
creator: Benjamin J. Ricketts, James F. Steiner, Cecilia Garraffo, Ronald A. Remillard, Daniela Huppenkothen
description: Abstract Black hole X-ray binary systems (BHBs) contain a close companion star accreting onto a stellar-mass black hole. A typical BHB undergoes transient outbursts during which it exhibits a sequence of long-lived spectral states, each of which is relatively stable. GRS 1915+105 is a unique BHB that exhibits an unequaled number and variety of distinct variability patterns in X-rays.

title: Closed String Radiation from the Interaction of the Moving D p p -branes with Background Fields
description: Abstract At first, we derive a boundary state, associated with a moving D p p -brane, in the presence of the Kalb-Ramond field and a U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge potential. Then, from the interaction of such D p p -branes, we obtain the radiation amplitude for a massless closed string.

title: FewShotTextGCN: K-hop neighborhood regularization for few-shot learning on graphs
creator: Niels van der Heijden Ekaterina Shutova Helen Yannakoudakis
description: Abstract We present FewShotTextGCN, a novel method designed to effectively utilize the properties of word–document graphs for improved learning in low-resource settings. We introduce K-hop Neighborhood Regularization, a regularizer for heterogeneous graphs, and show that it stabilizes and improves learning when only a few training samples are available.

title: ArchEnemy: Removing scattered-light glitches from gravitational wave data.
creator: Arthur E. Tolley, Gareth S. Cabourn Davies, Ian W. Harry, Andrew P. Lundgren
description: Abstract Data recorded by gravitational wave detectors includes many non-astrophysical transient noise bursts, the most common of which is caused by scattered-light within the detectors. These so-called “glitches” in the data impact the ability to both observe and characterize incoming gravitational wave signals.

title: Early stages of Galilean moon formation in a water-depleted environment
creator: Olivier Mousis, Antoine Schneeberger, Jonathan I. Lunine, Christopher R. Glein, Alexis Bouquet, Steven D. Vance
description: Abstract Résumé A key feature of the Galilean satellite system is its monotonic decrease in bulk density with distance from Jupiter, indicating an ice mass fraction that is zero in the innermost moon Io, and about half in the outer moons Ganymede and Callisto.

title: The formal seesaw mechanism of Majorana neutrinos with unbroken gauge symmetry
description: Abstract We reformulate the canonical seesaw mechanism in the case that the electroweak gauge symmetry is unbroken, and show that it can formally work and allow us to derive an exact seesaw formula for the light and heavy Majorana neutrinos.

title: Multi-Tenant Optimization For Few-Shot Task-Oriented FAQ Retrieval
creator: Asha VishwanathanVerloop.io asha@verloop.io Rajeev Unnikrishnan WarrierVerloop.io rajeev@verloop.io, Gautham Vadakkekara SureshVerloop.io gautham.suresh09@yahoo.com, Chandra Shekhar KandpalVerloop.io chandrashekhar1503@gmail.com
description: Abstract † † footnotetext: * Work done while the authors were working at Verloop.io Business-specific Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) retrieval in task-oriented dialog systems poses unique challenges vis-à-vis community based FAQs. Each FAQ question represents an intent which is usually an umbrella term for many related user queries.

title: ExaRanker: Explanation-Augmented Neural Ranker
creator: Fernando Ferraretto, Thiago Laitz, Roberto Lotufo, Rodrigo Nogueira
description: Abstract Recent work has shown that inducing a large language model (LLM) to generate explanations prior to outputting an answer is an effective strategy to improve performance on a wide range of reasoning tasks. In this work, we show that neural rankers also benefit from explanations. We use LLMs such as GPT-3.

title: Moderate deviations for functionals over infinitely many Rademacher random variables
creator: Marius Butzek, Peter Eichelsbacher, Benedikt Rednoß
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marius Butzek, Peter Eichelsbacher, Benedikt Rednoß. In this paper, moderate deviations for normal approximation of functionals over infinitely many Rademacher random variables are derived. They are based on a bound for the Kolmogorov distance between a general Rademacher functional and a Gaussian random variable, continued by an intensive study of the behavior of operators from the Malliavin–Stein method along with the moment generating function of the mentioned functional. As applications, subgraph counting in the Erdős–Rényi random graph and infinite weighted 2-runs are studied.

title: Phase proper orthogonal decomposition of non-stationary turbulent flow
creator: Yisheng Zhang (张益盛), Azur Hodžić, Fabien Evrard, Berend Van Wachem, Clara M. Velte
description: Abstract A phase proper orthogonal decomposition (Phase POD) method is demonstrated, utilizing phase averaging for the decomposition of spatio-temporal behaviour of statistically non-stationary turbulent flows in an optimized manner. The proposed Phase POD method is herein applied to a periodically forced statistically non-stationary lid-driven cavity flow, implemented using the snapshot proper orthogonal decomposition algorithm.

title: Randomized Benchmarking using Non-Destructive Readout in a 2D Atom Array
creator: B. Nikolov, E. Diamond-Hitchcock, J. Bass, N.L.R. Spong, J.D. Pritchard
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by B. Nikolov, E. Diamond-Hitchcock, J. Bass, N.L.R. Spong, J.D. Pritchard. Neutral atoms are a promising platform for scalable quantum computing, however prior demonstration of high fidelity gates or low-loss readout methods have employed restricted numbers of qubits. Using randomized benchmarking of microwave-driven single-qubit gates, we demonstrate average gate errors of 7 ​ ( 2 ) × 10 − 5 7(2)\times 10^{-5} on a 225 site atom array using conventional, destructive readout.

title: 3D Tooth Mesh Segmentation with Simplified Mesh Cell Representation
creator: Ananya Jana, Hrebesh Molly subhash, Dimitris Metaxas
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ananya Jana, Hrebesh Molly subhash, Dimitris Metaxas. Manual tooth segmentation of 3D tooth meshes is tedious and there is variations among dentists. Several deep learning based methods have been proposed to perform automatic tooth mesh segmentation. Many of the proposed tooth mesh segmentation algorithms summarize the mesh cell as - the cell center or barycenter, the normal at barycenter, the cell vertices and the normals at the cell vertices.

title: Nonequilibrium Seebeck effect and thermoelectric efficiency of Kondo-correlated molecular junctions
creator: Anand Manaparambil, Ireneusz Weymann
description: Abstract We theoretically study the nonequilibrium thermoelectric transport properties of a strongly-correlated molecule (or quantum dot) embedded in a tunnel junction. Assuming that the coupling of the molecule to the contacts is asymmetric, we determine the nonlinear current driven by the voltage and temperature gradients by using the perturbation theory.

title: Gate-controlled Magnetotransport and Electrostatic Modulation of Magnetism in 2D magnetic semiconductor CrPS 4
creator: Fan Wu, Marco Gibertini, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ignacio Gutiérrez-Lezama, Nicolas Ubrig, Alberto F. Morpurgo
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Fan Wu, Marco Gibertini, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ignacio Gutiérrez-Lezama, Nicolas Ubrig, Alberto F. Morpurgo. Using field-effect transistors (FETs) to explore atomically thin magnetic semiconductors with transport measurements is difficult, because the very narrow bands of most 2D magnetic semiconductors cause carrier localization, preventing transistor operation. Here, we show that exfoliated layers of CrPS 4 –a 2D layered antiferromagnetic semiconductor whose bandwidth approaches 1 eV– allow the realization of FETs that operate properly down to cryogenic temperature.

title: Central support for triangulated categories
creator: Henning Krause
description: Abstract . For any essentially small triangulated category the centre of its lattice of thick subcategories is introduced; it is a spatial frame and yields a notion of central support. A relative version of this centre recovers the support theory for tensor triangulated categories and provides a universal notion of cohomological support.

title: STRUCTURAL INSULATORS AND PROMOTORS IN NETWORKS UNDER GENERIC PROBLEM-SOLVING DYNAMICS
creator: JOHANNES FALK †, EDWIN EICHLER ‡§, KATJA WINDT ‡¶ and MARC-THORSTEN HÜTT †
description: Abstract The collective coordination of distributed tasks in a complex system can be represented as decision dynamics on a graph. This abstract representation allows studying the performance of local decision heuristics as a function of task complexity and network architecture. Here we identify hard-to-solve and easy-to-solve networks in a social differentiation task within the basic model of small-world graphs.

title: Robot Subset Selection for Swarm Lifetime Maximization in Computation Offloading with Correlated Data Sources
creator: Siqi Zhang, Na Yi, Yi Ma 5GIC and 6GIC, Institute for Communication Systems, University of Surrey, Guildford, UK, GU2 7XHEmails: (s.zhang, n.yi, y.ma)@surrey.ac.uk
description: Abstract Consider robot swarm wireless networks where mobile robots offload their computing tasks to a computing server located at the mobile edge. Our aim is to maximize the swarm lifetime through efficient exploitation of the correlation between distributed data sources. The optimization problem is handled by selecting appropriate robot subsets to send their sensed data to the server.

title: Understanding and Improving Deep Graph Neural Networks: A Probabilistic Graphical Model Perspective
creator: Jiayuan Chen, Xiang Zhang, Yinfei Xu, Tianli Zhao, Renjie Xie, Wei Xu
description: Abstract Recently, graph-based models designed for downstream tasks have significantly advanced research on graph neural networks (GNNs). GNN baselines based on neural message-passing mechanisms such as GCN and GAT perform worse as the network deepens. Therefore, numerous GNN variants have been proposed to tackle this performance degradation problem, including many deep GNNs.

title: Optomechanical feedback cooling of a 5 mm-long torsional mode
creator: Dianqiang Su, Yuan Jiang, Pablo Solano, Luis A. Orozco, John Lawall, Yanting Zhao
description: Abstract We report three orders of magnitude optical cooling of the fundamental torsional mode of a 5 mm-long, 550 nm diameter optical nanofiber. The rotation of the nanofiber couples to the polarization of guided laser fields. We use a weak laser probe to monitor the rotation, and use feedback to modulate the polarization of an auxiliary drive laser providing torque.

title: A Provable Splitting Approach for Symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization
creator: Xiao Li, Zhihui Zhu, Qiuwei Li, Kai Liu
description: Abstract The symmetric Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF), a special but important class of the general NMF, has found numerous applications in data analysis such as various clustering tasks. Unfortunately, designing fast algorithms for the symmetric NMF is not as easy as for its nonsymmetric counterpart, since the latter admits the splitting property that allows state-of-the-art alternating-type algorithms.

title: Tracking Different Ant Species: An Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Framework and a Dataset for Multi-object Tracking
creator: Chamath Abeysinghe, Chris Reid, Hamid Rezatofighi, Bernd Meyer
description: Abstract Tracking individuals is a vital part of many experiments conducted to understand collective behaviour. Ants are the paradigmatic model system for such experiments but their lack of individually distinguishing visual features and their high colony densities make it extremely difficult to perform reliable tracking automatically. Additionally, the wide diversity of their species’ appearances makes a generalized approach even harder.

title: Congruences for the difference of even and odd number of parts of the cubic and some analogous partition functions Thanks: 2020 Mathematics Subject Classifications. 11P83, 05A17. Keywords and phrases. Partitions, Cubic partitions, Congruence.
creator: Nayandeep Deka Baruah, Abhishek Sarma
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nayandeep Deka Baruah, Abhishek Sarma. Partitions wherein the even parts appear in two different colours are known as cubic partitions. Recently, Merca introduced and studied the function A ⁡ ( n ) A(n) , which is defined as the difference between the number of cubic partitions of n n into an even number of parts and the number of cubic partitions of n n into an odd number of parts.

title: Integrated multiresonator quantum memory
creator: N S Perminov, S A Moiseev
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by N S Perminov, S A Moiseev. We develop the integrated efficient multiresonator quantum memory scheme based on a system of three interacting resonators coupled through a common resonator to an external waveguide via switchable coupler. It is shown that high-precision parameter matching based on the step-by-step optimization makes it possible to efficiently store the signal field and on demand retrieval the signal at specified time moments. Possible experimental implementations and practical applications of the proposed quantum memory scheme are discussed.

title: Global asymmetry in Δ \Delta X variations during the 06 April 2000 geomagnetic storm: Relative roles of IMF B z B_{z} and B y B_{y}
description: Abstract This investigation is directed to understand the asymmetry in Δ \Delta X variations caused due to the relative roles played by IMF B z B_{z} and IMF B y B_{y} in a particular interval (22:22 - 22:55 UT), during the main phase of a strong geomagnetic storm event of April 06, 2000 ( A p A_{p} = 236).

title: ARDIAS: AI-Enhanced Research Management, Discovery, and Advisory System
creator: Debayan Banerjee, Seid Muhie Yimam, Sushil Awale, Chris Biemann
description: Abstract In this work, we present ARDIAS, a web-based application that aims to provide researchers with a full suite of discovery and collaboration tools. ARDIAS currently allows searching for authors and articles by name and gaining insights into the research topics of a particular researcher.

title: Scattering-matrix approach for a quantitative evaluation of the topological protection in valley photonic crystals
creator: Gaëtan Lévêque, Yan Pennec, Pascal Szriftgiser, Alberto Amo, Alejandro Martínez
description: Abstract The realization of photonic crystal waveguides with topological protection enables robust light propagation against defect-induced scattering. It should allow the design of very compact devices by exploiting guiding through sharp bends with low losses and back-reflection. In this work, we use valley-topological triangular resonators coupled to an input waveguide to evaluate the quality of the topological protection.

title: Leveraging Planning Landmarks for Hybrid Online Goal Recognition
creator: Nils Wilken, Lea Cohausz, Johannes Schaum, Stefan Lüdtke, Christian Bartelt, Heiner Stuckenschmidt
description: Abstract Goal recognition is an important problem in many application domains (e.g., pervasive computing, intrusion detection, computer games, etc.). In many application scenarios it is important that goal recognition algorithms can recognize goals of an observed agent as fast as possible and with minimal domain knowledge.

title: A Method For Eliminating Contour Errors In Self-Encoder Reconstructed Images
creator: @ David S. Hippocampus
description: Abstract In industry, products in the same product line are mostly similar. It is often a normal idea to use a self-encoder to reconstruct the image [ 1 , 2 ] in order to find product defects or foreign bodies in a differential way [ 3 , 4 ] .

title: Stray field computation by inverted finite elements: a new method in micromagnetic simulations
creator: Tahar Z. BOULMEZAOUD 1,2,3, Keltoum KALICHE 1,3
description: Abstract . In this paper, we propose a new method for computing the stray-field and the corresponding energy for a given magnetization configuration. Our approach is based on the use of inverted finite elements and does not need any truncation. After analyzing the problem in an appropriate functional framework, we describe the method and we prove its convergence.

title: Hubbard bands, Mott transition and deconfinement in strongly correlated systems
creator: V. Yu. Irkhin
description: Abstract The problem of deconfinement phases in strongly correlated systems is discussed. In space-time dimension d = 3 + 1 d=3+1 , a competition of confinement and Coulomb phases occurs, but in d = 2 + 1 d=2+1 the confining phase dominates owing to monopole proliferation, but gapless fermion excitations can change the situation.

title: Aggregating heavy-tailed random vectors: from finite sums to Lévy processes
creator: Bikramjit Das, Vicky Fasen-Hartmann
description: Abstract The tail behavior of aggregates of heavy-tailed random vectors is known to be determined by the so-called principle of “one large jump”, be it for finite sums, random sums, or, Lévy processes. We establish that, in fact, a more general principle is at play.

title: The Hubble constant tension: current status and future perspectives through new cosmological probes
creator: Gaetano Lambiase
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Gaetano Lambiase. The Hubble constant ( H 0 H_{0} ) tension is one of the major open problems in modern cosmology. This tension is the discrepancy, ranging from 4 to 6 σ \sigma , between the H 0 H_{0} value estimated locally with the combination of Supernovae Ia (SNe Ia) + Cepheids and the cosmological H 0 H_{0} obtained through the study of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation. The approaches adopted in [ 1 ] and [ 2 ] are introduced.

title: Connecting metrics for shape-texture knowledge in computer vision
creator: Tiago Oliveira, Tiago Marques, Arlindo L. Oliveira
description: Abstract Modern artificial neural networks, including convolutional neural networks and vision transformers, have mastered several computer vision tasks, including object recognition. However, there are many significant differences between the behavior and robustness of these systems and of the human visual system.

title: Strongly proper connected coloring of graphs
creator: Michał Dębski, Jarosław Grytczuk, Paweł Naroski, Małgorzata Śleszyńska-Nowak
description: Abstract We study a new variant of connected coloring of graphs based on the concept of strong edge coloring (every color class forms an induced matching). In particular, an edge-colored path is strongly proper if its color sequence does not contain identical terms within a distance of at most two.

title: Automated multilingual detection of Pro-Kremlin propaganda in newspapers and Telegram posts
creator: Veronika Solopova, Oana-Iuliana Popescu, Christoph Benzmüller, Tim Landgraf
description: Abstract The full-scale conflict between the Russian Federation and Ukraine generated an unprecedented amount of news articles and social media data reflecting opposing ideologies and narratives. These polarized campaigns have led to mutual accusations of misinformation and fake news, shaping an atmosphere of confusion and mistrust for readers worldwide.

title: Convergence of the solutions of the nonlinear discounted Hamilton–Jacobi equation: The central role of Mather measures.
creator: Qinbo Chen, Albert Fathi, Maxime Zavidovique, Jianlu Zhang
description: Abstract Given a continuous Hamiltonian H : ( x , p , u ) ↦ H ⁡ ( x , p , u ) H:(x,p,u)\mapsto H(x,p,u) defined on T ∗ ​ M × ℝ T^{*}M\times\mathbb{R} , where M M is a closed connected manifold, we study viscosity solutions, u λ : M → ℝ u_{\lambda}:M\to\mathbb{R} , of discounted equations: H

title: The quark propagator and quark-gluon vertex from lattice QCD at finite temperature
creator: Orlando Oliveira
description: Abstract The quark-gluon vertex is an important object of QCD. Studies have shown that this quantity is relevant for the dynamical chiral symmetry breaking pattern in the vacuum. The goal of our project is to obtain the quark-gluon vertex at finite temperature around the deconfinement/chiral transition using the tools provided by lattice QCD.

title: The Bogomolov multiplier of groups of order p 7 p^{7} and exponent p p
creator: Zeinab Araghi Rostami, Mohsen Parvizi, Peyman Niroomand
description: Abstract . In this paper, the Bogomolov multiplier of p p -groups of order p 7 p^{7} ( p > 2 p>2 ) and exponent p p is given. 1. Introduction Let K be a field, G be a finite group, and V be a faithful representation of G over K .

title: Early life exposure to measles and later-life outcomes: Evidence from the introduction of a vaccine Thanks: We gratefully acknowledge funding of this project from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme, grant agreement no. 851725
creator: Gerard J. van den Berg, Stephanie von Hinke, Nicolai Vitt
description: Abstract Until the mid 1960s, the UK experienced regular measles epidemics, with the vast majority of children being infected in early childhood. The introduction of a measles vaccine substantially reduced its incidence. The first part of this paper examines the long-term human capital and health effects of this change in the early childhood disease environment.

title: Hierarchical Regularizers for Reverse Unrestricted Mixed Data Sampling Regressions
creator: Alain Hecq Marie Ternes Ines Wilms
description: Abstract Reverse Unrestricted MIxed DAta Sampling (RU-MIDAS) regressions are used to model high-frequency responses by means of low-frequency variables. However, due to the periodic structure of RU-MIDAS regressions, the dimensionality grows quickly if the frequency mismatch between the high- and low-frequency variables is large. Additionally the number of high-frequency observations available for estimation decreases.

title: Succinct Planar Encoding with Minor Operations
creator: Frank Kammer, Johannes Meintrup
description: Abstract Let G G be an unlabeled planar and simple n n -vertex graph. Unlabeled graphs are graphs where the label-information is either not given or lost during the construction of data-structures. We present a succinct encoding of G G that provides induced-minor operations, i.e., edge contractions and vertex deletions.

title: Banker Online Mirror Descent: A Universal Approach for Delayed Online Bandit Learning
creator: Jiatai Huang, Yan Dai, Longbo Huang
description: Abstract We propose Banker Online Mirror Descent ( Banker-OMD ), a novel framework generalizing the classical Online Mirror Descent (OMD) technique in the online learning literature. The Banker-OMD framework almost completely decouples feedback delay handling and the task-specific OMD algorithm design, thus facilitating the design of new algorithms capable of efficiently and robustly handling feedback delays.

title: Stochastic particle transport by deep-water irregular breaking waves
creator: D. Eeltink 1,2,3, R. Calvert 4,5, J.E. Swagemakers 4, Qian Xiao 2, T.S. van den Bremer 2,4
description: Abstract Correct prediction of particle transport by surface waves is crucial in many practical applications such as search and rescue or salvage operations and pollution tracking and clean-up efforts. Recent results by Deike et al. 2017 and Pizzo et al. 2019 have indicated transport by deep-water breaking waves is enhanced compared to non-breaking waves.

title: Model-independent search for the presence of new physics in events including H → γ ​ γ H\rightarrow\gamma\gamma with s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC
description: Abstract A model-independent search for new physics leading to final states containing a Higgs boson, with a mass of 125.09 GeV, decaying to a pair of photons is performed with 139 fb -1 of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV p ​ p pp collision data recorded by the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider at CERN.

title: Symplectomorphisms and spherical objects in the conifold smoothing
creator: Ailsa Keating, Ivan Smith
description: Abstract . Let X X denote the ‘conifold smoothing’, the symplectic Weinstein manifold which is the complement of a smooth conic in T ∗ ​ S 3 T^{*}S^{3} , or equivalently the plumbing of two copies of T ∗ ​ S 3 T^{*}S^{3} along a Hopf link.

title: LTL Reactive Synthesis with a Few Hints Thanks: This work was partially supported by the Fonds de la Recherche Scientifique – F.R.S.-FNRS under the MIS project F451019F and by the ASP-Fellowship grant. Affiliation: Université libre de Bruxelles, Brussels, Belgium
creator: Mrudula Balachander, Emmanuel Filiot, Jean-François Raskin
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mrudula Balachander, Emmanuel Filiot, Jean-François Raskin. We study a variant of the problem of synthesizing Mealy machines that enforce LTL specifications against all possible behaviours of the environment including hostile ones . In the variant studied here, the user provides the high level LTL specification φ \varphi of the system to design, and a set E E of examples of executions that the solution must produce. Our synthesis algorithm works in two phases.

title: Prediction of COVID-19 by Its Variants using Multivariate Data-driven Deep Learning Models
creator: Akhmad Dimitri Baihaqi, Novanto Yudistira, Edy Santoso
description: Abstract The Coronavirus Disease 2019 or the COVID-19 pandemic has swept almost all parts of the world since the first case was found in Wuhan, China, in December 2019. With the increasing number of COVID-19 cases in the world, SARS-CoV-2 has mutated into various variants.

title: Discriminator-free Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Multi-label Image Classification
creator: Inder Pal Singh, Enjie Ghorbel, Anis Kacem, Arunkumar Rathinam, Djamila Aouada
description: Abstract In this paper, a discriminator-free adversarial-based Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) for Multi-Label Image Classification (MLIC) referred to as DDA-MLIC is proposed. Recently, some attempts have been made for introducing adversarial-based UDA methods in the context of MLIC. However, these methods, which rely on an additional discriminator subnet present one major shortcoming.

title: Incentive-weighted Anomaly Detection for False Data Injection Attacks Against Smart Meter Load Profiles
creator: \au Martin Higgins 1* , \au Bruce Stephen 2 , and \au David Wallom 1
description: Abstract Spot pricing is often suggested as a method of increasing demand-side flexibility in electrical power load. However, few works have considered the vulnerability of spot pricing to financial fraud via false data injection (FDI) style attacks. In this paper, we consider attacks which aim to alter the consumer load profile to exploit intraday price dips.

title: The upcoming spectroscopic powerhouses at the Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes
creator: Balcells, M.
description: Abstract Abstract The Isaac Newton Group of Telescopes is completing a strategic change for the scientific use of its two telescopes, the 4.2-m William Herschel Telescope (WHT) and the 2.5-m Isaac Newton Telescope (INT). After more than 30 years operating as multi-purpose telescopes, the telescopes will soon complete their shift to nearly-single instrument operation dominated by large surveys.

title: Clueless: A Tool C haracterising Va lue s L eaking as Addr ess es CCS: Security and privacy Side-channel analysis and countermeasures CCS: Security and privacy Information flow control
creator: Xiaoyue Chen, Pavlos Aimoniotis, Stefanos Kaxiras
description: Abstract . Clueless is a binary instrumentation tool that characterises explicit cache side channel vulnerabilities of programs. It detects the transformation of data values into addresses by tracking dynamic instruction dependencies. Clueless tags data values in memory if it discovers that they are used in address calculations to further access other data.

title: A Mathematical Programming approach to Overlapping community detection by cluster’s Shapley value
creator: Stefano Benati, Justo Puerto, Antonio M. Rodríguez-Chía, Francisco Temprano
description: Abstract We propose a new model to detect the overlapping communities of a network that is based on cooperative games and mathematical programming. More specifically, communities are defined as stable coalitions of a weighted graph community game and they are revealed as the optimal solution of a mixed-integer linear programming problem.

title: Extended Nullstellensatz proof systems Thanks: Sokolovská 83, Prague, 186 75, The Czech Republic, krajicek@karlin.mff.cuni.cz
creator: Jan Krajíček
description: Abstract For a finite set ℱ {\cal F} of polynomials from 𝐅 p ​ [ x ¯ ] {{{{\mathbf{F}}}_{p}}[\overline{x}]} ( p p is a fixed prime) containing all polynomials x 2 − x x^{2}-x , a Nullstellensatz proof of the unsolvability of the system f = 0 , all ​ f ∈ ℱ f=0\ ,\ \mbox{ all }f\in{\cal F} in

title: Excited-State Phase Diagram of a Ferromagnetic Quantum Gas
creator: B. Meyer-Hoppe 1, F. Anders 1, P. Feldmann 2,3,4, L. Santos 2, C. Klempt 1
description: Abstract The ground-state phases of a quantum many-body system are characterized by an order parameter, which changes abruptly at quantum phase transitions when an external control parameter is varied. Interestingly, these concepts may be extended to excited states, for which it is possible to define equivalent excited-state quantum phase transitions.

title: Probing Taxonomic and Thematic Embeddings for Taxonomic Information
creator: Filip Klubička, John D. Kelleher
description: Abstract Modelling taxonomic and thematic relatedness is important for building AI with comprehensive natural language understanding. The goal of this paper is to learn more about how taxonomic information is structurally encoded in embeddings. To do this, we design a new hypernym-hyponym probing task and perform a comparative probing study of taxonomic and thematic SGNS and GloVe embeddings.

title: (Almost Full) EFX for Three (and More) Types of Agents
creator: Pratik Ghosal Vishwa Prakash HV Indian Institute of Technology Palakkad Chennai Mathematical Institute pratik@iitpkd.ac.in vishwa@cmi.ac.in Prajakta Nimbhorkar Nithin Varma Chennai Mathematical Institute University of Cologne, Germany prajakta@cmi.ac.in nithvarma@gmail.com
description: Abstract We study the problem of determining an envy-free allocation of indivisible goods among multiple agents with additive valuations. EFX, which stands for envy-freeness up to any good, is a well-studied relaxation of the envy-free allocation problem and has been shown to exist for specific scenarios.

title: Vanishing Theorem for Hodge Ideals on Smooth Hypersurfaces
creator: Anh Duc Vo
description: Abstract . We use a Koszul-type resolution to prove a weak version of Bott’s vanishing theorem for smooth hypersurfaces in ℙ n \mathbb{P}^{n} and use this result to prove a vanishing theorem for Hodge ideals associated to an effective Cartier divisor on a hypersurface. This extends an earlier result of Mustaţă and Popa. 1.

title: Adaptive enrichment trial designs using joint modeling of longitudinal and time-to-event data
creator: Abigail J. Burdon, Richard D. Baird, Thomas Jaki
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Abigail J. Burdon, Richard D. Baird, Thomas Jaki. Adaptive enrichment allows for pre-defined patient subgroups of interest to be investigated throughout the course of a clinical trial. Many trials which measure a long-term time-to-event endpoint often also routinely collect repeated measures on biomarkers. In this work, we present a joint model for longitudinal and time-to-event data and two methods for creating standardised statistics based on this joint model.

title: An Overview on Cloud Distributed Databases for Business Environments
creator: 1 st Allan Vikiru, 2 nd Mfadhili Muiruri, 3 rd Ismail Ateya
description: Abstract Cloud-based distributed databases are a popular choice for many current applications, especially those that run over the Internet. By incorporating distributed database systems within cloud environments, it has enabled businesses to scale operations to a global level, all while achieving desired standards of system reliability, availability, and responsiveness.

title: Momentum-dependent flow correlations in deformed nuclei at collision energies available at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
creator: Rupam Samanta, Piotr Bożek
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rupam Samanta, Piotr Bożek. Flow fluctuations in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collision can be probed by studying the momentum dependent correlations or the factorization-breaking coefficients between flow harmonics in separate kinematic bins (transverse momentum p p or pseudorapidity η \eta ). We study such factorization-breaking coefficients for collisions of deformed 238 U+ 238 U nuclei to see the effect of the nuclear deformation on momentum dependent coefficients.

title: MLPGradientFlow: going with the flow of multilayer perceptrons (and finding minima fast and accurately)
creator: Johanni Brea, Flavio Martinelli, Berfin Şimşek, Wulfram Gerstner
description: Abstract MLPGradientFlow is a software package to solve numerically the gradient flow differential equation θ ˙ = − ∇ ℒ ​ ( θ , 𝒟 ) \dot{\theta}=-\nabla\mathcal{L}(\theta;\mathcal{D}) , where θ \theta are the parameters of a multi-layer perceptron, 𝒟 \mathcal{D} is some data set, and ∇ ℒ \nabla\mathcal{L} is the gradient of a loss function.

title: Optical and near-infrared stellar activity characterization of the early M dwarf Gl 205 with SOPHIE and SPIRou
creator: P. Cortés-Zuleta, I. Boisse, B. Klein, E. Martioli, P. I. Cristofari, A. Antoniadis-Karnavas, J-F. Donati, X. Delfosse, C. Cadieux, N. Heidari, É. Artigau, S. Bellotti, X. Bonfils, A. Carmona, N. J. Cook, R. F. Díaz, R. Doyon, P. Fouqué, C. Moutou, P. Petit, T. Vandal, L. Acuña, L. Arnold, N. Astudi
description: Abstract Context. The stellar activity of M dwarfs is the main limitation for discovering and characterizing exoplanets orbiting them, since it induces quasi-periodic radial velocity (RV) variations. Aims. We aim to characterize the magnetic field and stellar activity of the early, moderately active, M dwarf Gl 205 in the optical and near-infrared (nIR) domains. Methods.

title: Energy-Delay Tradeoff in Helper-Assisted NOMA-MEC Systems: A Four-Sided Matching Algorithm
creator: Mengmeng Ren, Long Yang, Hai Jiang, Jian Chen, and Yuchen Zhou
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mengmeng Ren, Long Yang, Hai Jiang, Jian Chen, and Yuchen Zhou. This paper designs a helper-assisted resource allocation strategy in non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-enabled mobile edge computing (MEC) systems, in order to guarantee the quality of service (QoS) of the energy/delay-sensitive user equipments (UEs). To achieve a tradeoff between the energy consumption and the delay, we introduce a novel performance metric, called energy-delay tradeoff , which is defined as the weighted sum of energy consumption and delay.

title: On the Well-Posedness of a Fractional Stokes-Transport System
creator: Dimitri Cobb
description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Dimitri Cobb. Abstract

The purpose of this paper is to study the existence, uniqueness and lifespan of solutions for a fractional Stokes-Transport system. This problem should be understood as a model for sedimentation in a fluid where the viscosity law is given by a fractional Lapalce operator
(-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}
, with
\alpha=2
corresponding to the case of a normal viscous fluid, and
\alpha=0
reducing the problem to the Inviscid Incompressible Porous Media equation.

title: Towards a Unification of Logic and Information Theory
creator: Luis A. Lastras, Barry Trager, Jonathan Lenchner, Wojciech Szpankowski, Chai Wah Wu, Mark S. Squillante, Alexander Gray
description: Abstract Today, the vast majority of the world’s digital information is represented using the fundamental assumption, introduced by Claude Shannon in 1948, that “…the semantic aspects of communication are irrelevant to the engineering problem (of the design of communication systems)…”.

title: Polar magneto-optic Kerr and Faraday effects in finite periodic 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathcal{T} -symmetric systems
creator: Antonio Perez-Garrido, Peng Guo, Vladimir Gasparian, Esther Jódar
description: Abstract We discuss the anomalous behavior of the Faraday (transmission) and polar Kerr (reflection) rotation angles of the propagating light, in finite periodic parity-time ( 𝒫 ​ 𝒯 \mathcal{P}\mathcal{T} ) symmetric structures, consisting of N N cells. The unit cell potential is two complex δ \delta -potentials placed on both boundaries of the ordinary dielectric slab.

title: Values of p p -adic hypergeometric functions, and p p -adic analogue of Kummer’s linear identity
creator: Neelam Saikia
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Neelam Saikia. Let p p be an odd prime and 𝔽 p \mathbb{F}_{p} be the finite field with p p elements. This paper focuses on the study of values of a generic family of hypergeometric functions in the p p -adic setting which we denote by G 3 ​ n − 1 3 ​ n − 1 ​ ( p , t ) , {{}_{3n-1}G_{3n-1}}(p,t), where n ≥ 1 n\geq 1 and t ∈ 𝔽 p t\in\mathbb{F}_{p} .

title: Implicit Shape Model Trees: Recognition of 3-D Indoor Scenes and Prediction of Object Poses for Mobile Robots Journal: arXiv.org
creator: Pascal Meißner, Rüdiger Dillmann
description: Abstract We present an approach for mobile robots to recognize scenes in object arrangements distributed across cluttered environments. Recognition is enabled by intertwining the robot’s search for objects and the assignment of found objects to scenes. Our scene model called "Implicit Shape Model (ISM) trees" allows these two tasks to be solved jointly.

title: Constrained Expectation-Maximisation for inference of social graphs explaining online user-user interactions
creator: Effrosyni Papanastasiou, Anastasios Giovanidis
description: Abstract Current network inference algorithms fail to generate graphs with edges that can explain whole sequences of node interactions in a given dataset or trace . To quantify how well an inferred graph can explain a trace, we introduce feasibility , a novel quality criterion, and suggest that it is linked to the result’s accuracy.

title: RIS Meets Aerodynamic HAPS: A Multi-objective Optimization Approach
creator: Arman Azizi, Student Member, IEEE , Arman Farhang, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract In this letter, we propose a novel network architecture for integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) to establish connection between terrestrial ground stations which are unconnected due to blockage. We propose a new network framework where reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is mounted on an aerodynamic high altitude platform station (HAPS), referred to as aerodynamic HAPS-RIS.

title: Note on the conjugacy classes of elements and their centralizers for the free product of two groups
creator: Dan Burghelea
description: Abstract We describe the conjugacy classes of the elements of the free product of two groups and their centralizers and, as a consequence, we correct the calculation of the cyclic and periodic cyclic homology of the group ring of the free product of two groups given in a previous paper.

title: Investigating Strategies for Clause Recommendation
creator: Sagar Joshi \orcid 0000-0001-6095-9713, Sumanth Balaji \orcid 0000-0002-5669-7519, Jerrin Thomas, Aparna Garimella, Vasudeva Varma
description: Abstract Clause recommendation is the problem of recommending a clause to a legal contract, given the context of the contract in question and the clause type to which the clause should belong. With not much prior work being done toward the generation of legal contracts, this problem was proposed as a first step toward the bigger problem of contract generation.

title: The Clinical Trials Puzzle: How Network Effects Limit Drug Discovery
creator: Kishore Vasan, Deisy Morselli Gysi, Albert-László Barabási
description: Abstract The depth of knowledge offered by post-genomic medicine has carried the promise of new drugs, and cures for multiple diseases. To explore the degree to which this capability has materialized, we extract meta-data from 356,403 clinical trials spanning four decades, aiming to offer mechanistic insights into the innovation practices in drug discovery.

title: Powering an AI Chatbot with Expert Sourcing to Support Credible Health Information Access DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock
creator: Ziang Xiao, Q. Vera Liao, Michelle X. Zhou, Tyrone Grandison ∗, Yunyao Li ∗
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ziang Xiao, Q. Vera Liao, Michelle X. Zhou, Tyrone Grandison ∗, Yunyao Li ∗. During a public health crisis like the COVID-19 pandemic, a credible and easy-to-access information portal is highly desirable. It helps with disease prevention, public health planning, and misinformation mitigation.

title: Direct observation of magnon BEC in an out-of-plane magnetized yttrium iron garnet film
creator: G. A. Knyazev, A. N. Kuzmichev, P. E. Petrov, I. V. Savochkin, P. M. Vetoshko, V. I. Belotelov, Yu. M. Bunkov
description: Abstract Bose-Einstain condensation occurs at an appropriate density of bosonic particles, depending on their mass and temperature. We were able to experimentally observe the transition from the spin wave regime to the magnon Bose-Einstein condensed state (mBEC) with increasing magnon density by a microwave pumping. We used optical methods to register the spatial distribution of the magnon density and phase.

title: Transforming photon statistics through zero-photon subtraction
creator: C. M. Nunn, S. U. Shringarpure, T. B. Pittman
description: Abstract Zero-photon subtraction (ZPS) is a conditional measurement process that can reduce the mean photon number of quantum optical states without physically removing any photons. Here we show that ZPS can also be used to transform certain super-Poissonian states into sub-Poissonian states, and vice versa.

title: Efficient construction of involutory linear combinations of anti-commuting Pauli generators for large-scale iterative qubit coupled cluster calculations
creator: Ilya G. Ryabinkin, Andrew J. Jena, Scott N. Genin
description: Abstract We present an efficient method for construction of a fully anti-commutative set of Pauli generators (elements of the Pauli group) from a commutative set of operators that are composed exclusively from Pauli x ^ i \hat{x}_{i} operators (purely X generators) and sorted by an associated numerical measure, such as absolute energy gradients.

title: A weakly universal weighted cellular automaton in the heptagrid with 6 states
creator: Maurice Margenstern
description: Abstract In this paper, we prove that there is a weakly universal weighted cellular automaton in the heptagrid, the tessellation { 7 , 3 } \{7,3\} of the hyperbolic plane, with 6 states. The present paper improves a previous result with 7 states deposited on arXiv:2301.1091v1, arXiv:2301.1091v2 and on arXiv:2301.1091v3.

title: Controllable optical sideband generation by breaking mechanical Parity-Time symmetry
creator: Souvik Mondal, Kapil Debnath
description: Abstract The interaction between light and mechanical vibrations in a cavity is often exploited to produce higher order sidebands (HOS) /combs, which are used in optical communication networks, spectroscopy, and others. Although a considerable study of optomechanically induced HOS has been done, its proper control and manipulation using only continuous wave (CW) laser drive are still to be explored.

title: An Efficient Semi-Automated Scheme for Infrastructure LiDAR Annotation Thanks: indicates corresponding author: Pan He (mybestsonny@gmail.com)
creator: Aotian Wu, Pan He, Xiao Li, Ke Chen, Sanjay Ranka, Anand RangarajanModern Artificial Intelligence and Learning Technologies LabDepartment of Computer and Information Science and EngineeringThe University of Florida, Gainesville, Florida, USA
description: Abstract Most existing perception systems rely on sensory data acquired from cameras, which perform poorly in low light and adverse weather conditions. To resolve this limitation, we have witnessed advanced LiDAR sensors become popular in perception tasks in autonomous driving applications. Nevertheless, their usage in traffic monitoring systems is less ubiquitous.

title: Gain Recovery in Heavily Irradiated Low Gain Avalanche Detectors by High Temperature Annealing Note: The work was partly done in the framework of the RD50 collaboration. Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods A
creator: I. Mandić, V. Cindro, A. Gorišek, B. Hiti, A. Howard, Ž. Kljun, G. Kramberger, M. Maček Kržmanc, M. Mikuž, B. Novak
description: Abstract Studies of annealing at temperatures up to 450 ∘ C with Low Gin Avalnche Detectors (LGAD) irradiated with neutrons are described. It was found that the performance of lgads irradiated with 1.5e15 n/cm 2 was already improved at 5 minutes of annealing at 250 ∘ C.

title: Freezing transition and moments of moments of the Riemann zeta function
creator: Michael J. Curran
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Michael J. Curran. Moments of moments of the Riemann zeta function, defined by MoM T ​ ( k , β ) := 1 T ​ ∫ T 2 ​ T ( ∫ | h | ≤ ( log ⁡ T ) θ | ζ ⁡ ( 1 2 + i ​ t + i ​ h ) | 2 ​ β ​ 𝑑 h ) k ​ 𝑑 t \text{MoM}_{T}(k,\beta):=\frac{1}{T}\int_{T}^{2T}\Bigg(\int\displaylimits_{|h|\leq(\log T)^{\theta}}|\zeta(\tfrac{1}{2}+it+ih)|^{2\beta}~dh\Bigg)^{k}~dt where k , β ≥ 0 k,\beta\geq 0 and θ > − 1

title: The p p -arithmetic homology of mod p p representations of GL 2 ​ ( ℚ p ) \text{GL}_{2}(\mathbb{Q}_{p})
creator: Guillem Tarrach
description: Abstract . We compute the non-Eisenstein systems of Hecke eigenvalues contributing to the p p -arithmetic homology of irreducible smooth mod p p representations π \pi of GL 2 ​ ( ℚ p ) \text{GL}_{2}(\mathbb{Q}_{p}) and to the cohomology of their duals.

title: Testing Λ \Lambda CDM cosmology in a binned universe: anomalies in the deceleration parameter
creator: Erick Pastén, Víctor H. Cárdenas
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Erick Pastén, Víctor H. Cárdenas. We study the reconstructed deceleration parameter splitting the data in different redshift bins, fitting both a cosmographic luminosity distance and also assuming a flat Λ \Lambda CDM model, using the Pantheon+ sample of type Ia supernova data (SNIA). We observe tensions ∼ 2 ​ σ − 3 ​ σ \sim 2\sigma-3\sigma for different redshift and distance indicators if the full sample is used. However, those tensions disappear when the SNIA at z < 0.008 z<0.008 are removed.

title: Set-Theoretic and Type-Theoretic Ordinals Coincide PubID: pubid: 979-8-3503-3587-3/23/$31.00 ©2023 IEEE
creator: Tom de Jong 1 , Nicolai Kraus 1 , Fredrik Nordvall Forsberg 2 and Chuangjie Xu 3
description: Abstract In constructive set theory, an ordinal is a hereditarily transitive set. In homotopy type theory (HoTT), an ordinal is a type with a transitive, wellfounded, and extensional binary relation. We show that the two definitions are equivalent if we use (the HoTT refinement of) Aczel’s interpretation of constructive set theory into type theory.

title: 1D Convolutional neural networks and machine learning algorithms for spectral data classification with a case study for Covid-19
creator: Breno Aguiar Krohling, Renato A. Krohling
description: Abstract Machine and deep learning algorithms have increasingly been applied to solve problems in various areas of knowledge. Among these areas, Chemometrics has been benefited from the application of these algorithms in spectral data analysis. Commonly, algorithms such as Support Vector Machines and Partial Least Squares are applied to spectral datasets to perform classification and regression tasks.

title: The fate of infrared divergences in a finite formulation of field theory: QED revisited
creator: Jean-François Mathiot
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jean-François Mathiot. Within the framework of the recently proposed Taylor-Lagrange regularization procedure, we reanalyze the calculation of radiative corrections in Q ​ E ​ D QED at next to leading order. Starting from a well defined local bare Lagrangian, the use of this regularization procedure enables us to manipulate fully finite elementary amplitudes in the ultra-violet as well as infra-red regimes, in physical D = 4 D=4 space-time dimensions and for physical massless photons, as required by gauge invariance.

title: Topological black holes in higher derivative gravity
creator: Alena Pravdová, Vojtěch Pravda, Marcello Ortaggio
description: Abstract We study static black holes in quadratic gravity with planar and hyperbolic symmetry and non-extremal horizons. We obtain a solution in terms of an infinite power-series expansion around the horizon, which is characterized by two independent integration constants – the black hole radius and the strength of the Bach tensor at the horizon.

title: Distributed Control of Partial Differential Equations Using Convolutional Reinforcement Learning Journal: Physica D
creator: Sebastian Peitz, Jan Stenner, Vikas Chidananda, Oliver Wallscheid, Steven L. Brunton, Kunihiko Taira
description: Abstract We present a convolutional framework which significantly reduces the complexity and thus, the computational effort for distributed reinforcement learning control of dynamical systems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). Exploiting translational equivariances, the high-dimensional distributed control problem can be transformed into a multi-agent control problem with many identical, uncoupled agents.

title: The Dynamics of Co-orbital Giant Exomoons - Applications for the Kepler-1625 b and Kepler-1708 b Satellite Systems 2022 The Dynamics of Co-orbital Giant Exomoons - Applications for the Kepler-1625 b and Kepler-1708 b Satellite Systems – References
creator: R. A. Moraes G. Borderes-Motta O. C. Winter, D. C. Mourão
description: Abstract Exomoons are a missing piece of exoplanetary science. Recently, two promising candidates were proposed, Kepler-1625 b-I and Kepler-1708 b-I. While the latter still lacks a dynamical analysis of its stability, Kepler-1625 b-I has already been the subject of several studies regarding its stability and origin.

title: About Toroidal Model of Leptons in Space-Time Film Theory
creator: Alexander A. Chernitskii 1,2
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Alexander A. Chernitskii 1,2. Nonlinear field model of extremal space-time film is considered. Its space-localized solutions in toroidal coordinates with periodic dependence on time are investigated. An accordance between these soliton solutions and leptons is considered. \recdate March 10, 2022 1 Introduction In this paper, we consider toroidal particle-like solutions or particles-solitons of the space-time film equation [ 3 ] which can be associated with elementary particles, in particular, with leptons.

title: Fourier decay of equilibrium states for bunched attractors
creator: Gaétan Leclerc
description: Abstract Let M M be a closed manifold, and let f : M → M f:M\rightarrow M be a C 2 + α C^{2+\alpha} Axiom A diffeomorphism. Suppose that f f has an attractor Ω \Omega with codimension 1 stable lamination.

title: Fillers in Spoken Language Understanding: Computational and Psycholinguistic Perspectives
creator: Tanvi Dinkar, Chloé Clavel, Ioana Vasilescu
description: Abstract Disfluencies , or interruptions in the regular flow of speech are ubiquitous to spoken discourse. Fillers (‘‘uh’’, ‘‘um’’, …) are disfluencies that occur the most frequently compared to other kinds of disfluencies. Yet to the best of our knowledge, there isn’t a resource that brings together the research perspectives influencing Spoken Language Understanding (SLU) on these speech events.

title: Extragalactic CO emission lines in the CMB experiments: a forgotten signal and a foreground
creator: Abhishek S. Maniyar, Athanasia Gkogkou, William R. Coulton, Zack Li, Guilaine Lagache, Anthony R. Pullen
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Abhishek S. Maniyar, Athanasia Gkogkou, William R. Coulton, Zack Li, Guilaine Lagache, Anthony R. Pullen. High resolution cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments have allowed us to precisely measure the CMB temperature power spectrum down to very small scales (multipole ℓ ∼ 3000 \ell\sim 3000 ). Such measurements at multiple frequencies enable separating the primary CMB anisotropies with other signals like CMB lensing, thermal and kinematic Sunyaev-Zel’dovich effects (tSZ and kSZ), and cosmic infrared background (CIB).

title: Distribution of the threshold for the symmetric perceptron Thanks: Sah and Sawhney were supported by NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program DGE-1745302. Sah was supported by the PD Soros Fellowship. Sawhney was supported by the Churchill Foundation.
creator: Ashwin Sah, Mehtaab Sawhney
description: Abstract . We derive an explicit distribution for the threshold sequence of the symmetric binary perceptron with Gaussian disorder, proving that the critical window is of constant width. 1. Introduction We fix a real number \kappa>0 throughout the rest of this paper. Definition 1.1 . Let \Sigma_{n}=\{\pm 1\}^{n} .

title: Generalizability in Document Layout Analysis for Scientific Article Figure & Caption Extraction
creator: Jill Naiman
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jill Naiman. The lack of generalizability – in which a model trained on one dataset cannot provide accurate results for a different dataset – is a known problem in the field of document layout analysis. Thus, when a model is used to locate important page objects in scientific literature such as figures, tables, captions, and math formulas, the model often cannot be applied successfully to new domains.

title: Reconstruction of Fast Neutron Direction in Segmented Organic Detectors using Deep Learning
creator: Jun Woo Bae, Tingshiuan C. Wu and Igor Jovanovic
description: Abstract A method for reconstructing the direction of a fast neutron source using a segmented organic scintillator-based detector and deep learning model is proposed and analyzed. The model is based on recurrent neural network, which can be trained by a sequence of data obtained from an event recorded in the detector and suitably pre-processed.

title: JWST Discovery of Dust Reservoirs in Nearby Type IIP Supernovae 2004et and 2017eaw JWST Discovery of Dust Reservoirs in Nearby Type IIP Supernovae 2004et and 2017eaw – References 2023
creator: Melissa Shahbandeh, Arkaprabha Sarangi, Tea Temim, Tamás Szalai, Ori D. Fox, Samaporn Tinyanont, Eli Dwek, Luc Dessart, Alexei V. Filippenko, Thomas G. Brink, Ryan J. Foley, Jacob Jencson, Justin Pierel, Szanna Zsíros, Armin Rest, WeiKang Zheng, Jennifer Andrews, Geoffrey C. Clayton, Kishalay De, Mi
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Melissa Shahbandeh, Arkaprabha Sarangi, Tea Temim, Tamás Szalai, Ori D. Fox, Samaporn Tinyanont, Eli Dwek, Luc Dessart, Alexei V. Filippenko, Thomas G. Brink, Ryan J. Foley, Jacob Jencson, Justin Pierel, Szanna Zsíros, Armin Rest, WeiKang Zheng, Jennifer Andrews, Geoffrey C. Clayton, Kishalay De, Mi. Supernova (SN) explosions have been sought for decades as a possible source of dust in the Universe, providing the seeds of galaxies, stars, and planetary systems.

title: Quantum anomaly detection in the latent space of proton collision events at the LHC
creator: Vasilis Belis ∗†, Kinga Anna Woźniak †, Ema Puljak †, Panagiotis Barkoutsos, Günther Dissertori, Michele Grossi, Maurizio Pierini, Florentin Reiter, Ivano Tavernelli, Sofia Vallecorsa
description: Abstract The ongoing quest to discover new phenomena at the LHC necessitates the continuous development of algorithms and technologies. Established approaches like machine learning, along with emerging technologies such as quantum computing show promise in the enhancement of experimental capabilities.

title: Updated High-Temperature Opacities for The Dartmouth Stellar Evolution Program and their Effect on the Jao Gap Location The Dartmouth Stellar Evolution Program (DSEP) ( Dotter et al. 2008 ) , BeautifulSoup ( Richardson 2007 ) , mechanize ( Chandra & Varanasi 2015 ) , FreeEOS ( Irwin 2012 ) , pyTOPSS
creator: Thomas M. Boudreaux, Brian C. Chaboyer
description: Abstract The Jao Gap, a 17 percent decrease in stellar density at M G ∼ {}_{G}\sim 10 identified in both Gaia DR2 and EDR3 data, presents a new method to probe the interior structure of stars near the fully convective transition mass.

title: Dark Radiation from Neutrino Mixing after Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
creator: Daniel Aloni, Melissa Joseph, Martin Schmaltz, Neal Weiner
description: Abstract Light dark fermions can mass mix with the Standard Model neutrinos. As a result, through oscillations and scattering, they can equilibrate in the early universe. Interactions of the dark fermion generically suppress such production at high temperatures but enhance it at later times.

title: Towards a Unified Model for Generating Answers and Explanations in Visual Question Answering
creator: Chenxi Whitehouse, Tillman Weyde, Pranava Madhyastha City, University of London {chenxi.whitehouse, t.e.weyde, pranava.madhyastha}@city.ac.uk
description: Abstract The field of visual question answering (VQA) has recently seen a surge in research focused on providing explanations for predicted answers. However, current systems mostly rely on separate models to predict answers and generate explanations, leading to less grounded and frequently inconsistent results.

title: The Tilting Space of Boundary Conformal Field Theories
creator: Christopher P. Herzog, Vladimir Schaub
description: Abstract In boundary conformal field theories, global symmetries can be broken by boundary conditions, generating a homogeneous conformal manifold. We investigate these geometries, showing they have a coset structure, and give fully worked out examples in the case of free fields of spin zero and one-half.

title: Role of ionizing background on the statistics of metal absorbers in hydrodynamical simulations 2022 Role of ionizing background on the statistics of metal absorbers in hydrodynamical simulations – References
creator: Sukanya Mallik, Raghunathan Srianand, Soumak Maitra, Prakash Gaikwad & Nishikanta Khandai
description: Abstract We study the statistical properties of O vi , C iv , and Ne viii absorbers at low- z z (i.e., z < 0.5 z<0.5 ) using Sherwood simulations with "WIND" only and "WIND+AGN" feedback and Massive black-II simulation that incorporates both "WIND" i.e. outflows driven by stellar feedback and AGN feedbacks.

title: Valuation of the Convertible Bonds under Penalty TF model using Finite Element Method
creator: Rakhymzhan Kazbek, Yogi Erlangga, Yerlan Amanbek, Dongming Wei
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rakhymzhan Kazbek, Yogi Erlangga, Yerlan Amanbek, Dongming Wei. In this paper, the TF system of two-coupled Black-Scholes equations for pricing the convertible bonds is solved numerically by using the P1 and P2 finite elements with the inequality constraints approximated by the penalty method. The corresponding finite element ODE system is numerically solved by using a modified Crank-Nicolson scheme, in which the non-linear system is solved at each time step by the Newton-Raphson method for non-smooth functions.

title: New charged anisotropic solution on paraboloidal spacetime
creator: Rinkal Patel, B. S. Ratanpal, D. M. Pandya
description: Abstract New exact solutions of Einstein’s field equations for charged stellar models by assuming linear equation of state P r = A ⁡ ( ρ − ρ a ) P_{r}=A(\rho-\rho_{a}) , where P r P_{r} is the radial pressure and ρ a \rho_{a} is the surface density.

title: Interpreting Knowledge-based Programs (Extended Version with Proofs) Thanks: A short version without proofs has been submitted to ESOP 23.
creator: Alexander Knapp, Heribert Mühlberger, Bernhard Reus
description: Abstract Knowledge-based programs specify multi-agent protocols with epistemic guards that abstract from how agents learn and record facts or information about other agents and the environment. Their interpretation involves a non-monotone mutual dependency between the evaluation of epistemic guards over the reachable states and the derivation of the reachable states depending on the evaluation of epistemic guards.

title: Monoidal envelopes and Grothendieck construction for dendroidal Segal objects
creator: David Kern
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Kern. We propose a construction of the monoidal envelope of ∞ \infty -operads in the model of Segal dendroidal spaces, and use it to define cocartesian fibrations of such. We achieve this by viewing the dendroidal category as a “plus construction” of the category of pointed finite sets, and work in the more general language of algebraic patterns for Segal conditions.

title: T − T- linear resistivity from magneto-elastic scattering: application to PdCrO 2
creator: J.F. Mendez-Valderrama, Evyatar Tulipman, Elina Zhakina, Andrew P. Mackenzie, Erez Berg, Debanjan Chowdhury
description: Abstract An electronic solid with itinerant carriers and localized magnetic moments represents a paradigmatic strongly correlated system. The electrical transport properties associated with the itinerant carriers, as they scatter off these local moments, has been scrutinized across a number of materials.

title: Full trajectory optimizing operator inference for reduced-order modeling using differentiable programming
creator: Surya Chakrabarti , Datta Gaitonde, Arvind T. Mohan, Daniel Livescu
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Surya Chakrabarti , Datta Gaitonde, Arvind T. Mohan, Daniel Livescu. Accurate and computationally inexpensive Reduced Order Models (ROMs) capable of forecasting turbulent flows can facilitate rapid design iterations and thus prove critical for predictive control strategies in engineering problems. Galerkin projection based Reduced Order Models (GP-ROMs), derived by projecting the Navier-Stokes equations on a truncated Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) basis, are popular because of their low computational costs and theoretical foundations in the governing fluid flow equations.

title: Nitrogen-enriched, highly-pressurized nebular clouds surrounding a super star cluster at cosmic noon
creator: Massimo Pascale, Liang Dai, Christopher F. McKee, Benny T.-H. Tsang
description: Abstract Strong lensing offers a precious opportunity for studying the formation and early evolution of super star clusters that are rare in our cosmic backyard. The Sunburst Arc, a lensed Cosmic Noon galaxy, hosts a young super star cluster with escaping Lyman continuum radiation.

title: Reflective Artificial Intelligence
creator: Peter R. Lewis, S , tefan Sarkadi
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Peter R. Lewis, S , tefan Sarkadi. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is about making computers that do the sorts of things that minds can do, and as we progress towards this goal, we tend to increasingly delegate human tasks to machines. However, AI systems usually do these tasks with an unusual imbalance of insight and understanding: new, deeper insights are present, yet many important qualities that a human mind would have previously brought to the activity are utterly absent.

title: Combination of searches for invisible decays of the Higgs boson using 139 fb -1 of proton-proton collision data at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13\penalty\ TeV collected with the ATLAS experiment
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . Many extensions of the Standard Model predict the production of dark matter particles at the LHC. Sufficiently light dark matter particles may be produced in decays of the Higgs boson that would appear invisible to the detector. This Letter presents a statistical combination of searches for H → invisible H\to\text{invisible} decays where multiple production modes of the Standard Model Higgs boson are considered.

title: Automatic Debiased Estimation with Machine Learning-Generated Regressors Thanks: Research supported by MICIN/AEI/10.13039/501100011033, grant CEX2021-001181-M, Comunidad de Madrid, grants EPUC3M11 (V PRICIT) and H2019/HUM-5891, and grant PID2021-127794NB-I00 (MCI/AEI/FEDER, UE).
creator: Juan Carlos Escanciano, Telmo J. Pérez-Izquierdo
description: Abstract Many parameters of interest in economics and other social sciences depend on generated regressors. Examples in economics include structural parameters in models with endogenous variables estimated by control functions and in models with sample selection, treatment effect estimation with propensity score matching, and marginal treatment effects.

title: Topology of singular foliation germs in ℂ 2 {\mathbb{C}}^{2} Thanks: D. Marín acknowledges financial support from the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities, through grant PID2021-125625NB-I00 and by the Agency for Management of University and Research Grants of Catalonia through t
creator: David Marín, Jean-François Mattei and Eliane Salem
description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by David Marín, Jean-François Mattei and Eliane Salem. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 37F75; Secondary 32M25, 32S50, 32S65, 34M Introduction The object of this survey is to give an overview on the topology of singularities of holomorphic foliation germs on ({\mathbb{C}}^{2},0) .

title: Flavor Leptogenesis During Reheating Era
creator: Arghyajit Datta, Rishav Roshan, Arunansu Sil
description: Abstract Recently, it has been shown that the presence of a non-instantaneous era of reheating can significantly alter the charged lepton(s) equilibration temperature(s) which plays important role in flavor leptogenesis. In this work, we extend the analysis to a more general situation where RHNs are also produced from the decay of the inflaton.

title: TranSOP: Transformer-based Multimodal Classification for Stroke Treatment Outcome Prediction
creator: Zeynel A. Samak, Philip Clatworthy, Majid Mirmehdi
description: Abstract Acute ischaemic stroke, caused by an interruption in blood flow to brain tissue, is a leading cause of disability and mortality worldwide. The selection of patients for the most optimal ischaemic stroke treatment is a crucial step for a successful outcome, as the effect of treatment highly depends on the time to treatment.

title: When Layers Play the Lottery, all Tickets Win at Initialization
creator: Artur Jordao, George Corrêa de Araújo, Helena de Almeida Maia, Helio Pedrini
description: Abstract Pruning is a standard technique for reducing the computational cost of deep networks. Many advances in pruning leverage concepts from the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH). LTH reveals that inside a trained dense network exists sparse subnetworks (tickets) able to achieve similar accuracy (i.e., win the lottery – winning tickets ).

title: On the inconsistency of separable losses for structured prediction
creator: Caio Corro
description: Abstract In this paper, we prove that separable negative log-likelihood losses for structured prediction are not necessarily Bayes consistent, or, in other words, minimizing these losses may not result in a model that predicts the most probable structure in the data distribution for a given input.

title: A Pseudo Plane-wave Gravitational Calibrator for Gravitational Wave Observatories
creator: M.P. Ross, J.H. Gundlach, E.G. Adelberger, C.M. Weller, E.A. Shaw, C. Gettings, J. Kissel, T. Mistry, L. Datrier, E. Daw, M. Hendry
description: Abstract The precisions of existing gravitational calibrators for gravitational wave observatories are limited by their dependence on the relative position between the calibrators and the observatory’s test masses. Here we present a novel geometry consisting of four quadrupole rotors placed at the vertices of a rectangle centered on the test mass.

title: Origin of ultra-low thermal conductivity in unconventional clathrates: Strong scattering from extremely low-frequency rattling modes
creator: Kamil M. Ciesielski, Brenden R. Ortiz, Lidia C. Gomes, Vanessa Meschke, Jesse M. Adamczyk, Tara L. Braden, Dariusz Kaczorowski, Elif Ertekin, Eric S. Toberer
description: Abstract Recent discoveries of materials with ultra-low thermal conductivity open a pathway to significant developments in the field of thermoelectricity. Here, we conduct a comparative study of three chemically similar antimonides to establish the root causes of their extraordinarily low thermal conductivity ( 0.4 − 0.6 0.4-0.6 Wm -1 K -1 at 525 K).

title: Graph Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence on Large Graphs
creator: Sanjukta Krishnagopal, Luana Ruiz
description: Abstract Graph neural networks (GNNs) achieve remarkable performance in graph machine learning tasks but can be hard to train on large-graph data, where their learning dynamics are not well understood. We investigate the training dynamics of large-graph GNNs using graph neural tangent kernels (GNTKs) and graphons.

title: Gatherplot: A Non-Overlapping Scatterplot
creator: Deokgun Park, Sung-Hee Kim, Niklas Elmqvist
description: Abstract Scatterplots are a common tool for exploring multidimensional datasets, especially in the form of scatterplot matrices (SPLOMs). However, scatterplots suffer from overplotting when categorical variables are mapped to one or two axes, or the same continuous variable is used for both axes. Previous methods such as histograms or violin plots use aggregation, which makes brushing and linking difficult.

title: Sub-Picosecond Carrier Dynamics Explored using Automated High-Throughput Studies of Doping Inhomogeneity within a Bayesian Framework
creator: Ruqaiya Al-Abri, Nawal Al Amairi, Stephen Church, Conor Byrne, Sudhakar Sivakumar, Alex Walton, Martin H. Magnusson, Patrick Parkinson

title: Efficiency in local differential privacy
creator: Lukas Steinberger
description: Abstract We develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency in regular parametric models when data confidentiality is ensured by local differential privacy (LDP). Even though efficient parameter estimation is a classical and well-studied problem in mathematical statistics, it leads to several non-trivial obstacles that need to be tackled when dealing with the LDP case.
