creator: Lianke Qin, Aravind Reddy, Zhao Song, Zhaozhuo Xu, Danyang Zhuo
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lianke Qin, Aravind Reddy, Zhao Song, Zhaozhuo Xu, Danyang Zhuo. In this paper, we propose Adam-Hash: an adaptive and dynamic multi-resolution hashing data-structure for fast pairwise summation estimation. Given a data-set X ⊂ ℝ d X\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} , a binary function f : ℝ d × ℝ d → ℝ f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R} , and a point y ∈ ℝ d y\in\mathbb{R}^{d} , the Pairwise Summation Estimate PSE X ​ ( y ) := 1 | X | ​ ∑ x ∈ X f ⁡ ( x

title: Effect of solar free oscillations on TianQin’s range acceleration noise
creator: Kun Liu, Chengjian Luo, Xuefeng Zhang
description: Abstract TianQin is a proposed space-based gravitational-wave detector mission to be deployed and operated in high Earth orbits. As a sequel to [Zhang et al . Phys. Rev. D 103, 062001 (2021)], we investigate a type of “orbital noise” in TianQin’s range acceleration that is caused by gravitational perturbation associated with solar free oscillations.

title: On the Schrödinger-Bopp-Podolsky system: Ground state & least energy nodal solutions with nonsmooth nonlinearity
creator: Anouar Bahrouni, Hlel Missaoui
description: Abstract In this paper, the following Schrödinger-Bopp-Podolsky system is studied { − △ ​ u + V ⁡ ( x ) ​ u + q 2 ​ ϕ ​ u = f ⁡ ( x , u ) , in ​ ℝ 3 , − △ ​ ϕ + a 2 ​ △ 2 ​ ϕ = 4 ​ π

title: A Moveable Beast: Partitioning Data and Compute for Computational Storage
creator: Aldrin Montana, Yuanqing Xue, Jeff LeFevre, Carlos Maltzahn, Josh Stuart, Philip Kufeldt, Peter Alvaro
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Aldrin Montana, Yuanqing Xue, Jeff LeFevre, Carlos Maltzahn, Josh Stuart, Philip Kufeldt, Peter Alvaro. Over the years, hardware trends have introduced a variety of heterogeneous compute units while also bringing network and storage bandwidths within an order of magnitude of memory subsystems. In response, developers have used increasingly exotic solutions to extract more performance from hardware; typically relying on static, design-time partitioning of their programs which cannot keep pace with storage systems that are layering compute units throughout deepening hierarchies of storage devices.

title: CAMeMBERT: Cascading Assistant-Mediated Multilingual BERT
creator: Dan DeGenaro, Jugal Kalita
description: Abstract Large language models having hundreds of millions, and even billions, of parameters have performed extremely well on a variety of natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Their widespread use and adoption, however, is hindered by the lack of availability and portability of sufficiently large computational resources.

title: Exploring dynamics of 𝑨 𝟒 A_{4} flavour symmetry using low scale seesaw mechanisms
creator: Kalpana Bora 1, Maibam Ricky Devi 1
description: Abstract Low scale seesaw models, like low scale type II, inverse (ISS), and linear seesaw (LSS) models provide an interesting mechanism to obtain light neutrino masses and mixings, as they can be tested in future TeV scale experiments. Discrete flavour symmetry groups like A 4 A_{4} can be incorporated to explain the flavour structure of particles.

title: Commitment with Signaling under Double-sided Information Asymmetry
creator: Tao Li, Quanyan Zhu
description: Abstract Information asymmetry in games enables players with the information advantage to manipulate others’ beliefs by strategically revealing information to other players. This work considers a double-sided information asymmetry in a Bayesian Stackelberg game, where the leader’s realized action, sampled from the mixed strategy commitment, is hidden from the follower. In contrast, the follower holds private information about his payoff.

title: Viscophoretic particle transport
creator: Vahid Khandan, 1 Vincent J. P. Boerkamp, 2 Abbas Jabermoradi, 2 Mattia Fontana, 2 Johannes Hohlbein, 2,3 Elisabeth Verpoorte, 1 Ryan C. Chiechi, 4, * and Klaus Mathwig 1,5,
description: Abstract Viscosity is a fundamental property of liquids and determines the diffusivity of suspended particles. A gradient in viscosity leads to a gradient in diffusivity, yet it is unknown whether such a gradient can lead to directed transport of particles.

title: Understanding and Improving the Role of Projection Head in Self-Supervised Learning
creator: Kartik Gupta, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Anton van den Hengel, Stephen Gould
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kartik Gupta, Thalaiyasingam Ajanthan, Anton van den Hengel, Stephen Gould. Self-supervised learning ( ssl ) aims to produce useful feature representations without access to any human-labeled data annotations. Due to the success of recent ssl methods based on contrastive learning, such as SimCLR, this problem has gained popularity. Most current contrastive learning approaches append a parametrized projection head to the end of some backbone network to optimize the InfoNCE objective and then discard the learned projection head after training.

title: Assignment of excitonic insulators in ab initio theories: the case of NiBr 2
creator: Stefano Di Sabatino, Alejandro Molina-Sánchez, Pina Romaniello, Davide Sangalli
description: Abstract In this work we perform a detailed first–principles analysis of the electronic and optical properties of NiBr 2 within the state–of–the–art G ​ W GW +BSE scheme to determine whether this system displays negative excitonic energies, which would identify it as an (half) excitonic insulator.

title: Study on the linearity of 20" dynode and MCP PMTs
creator: Yuekun Heng
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yuekun Heng. The linearity of charge response is an important feature of photomultiplier tubes (PMT) for physics measurements, especially the newly developed 20" MCP-PMT. In this paper, in addition to the traditional method of double light sources, we applied another relative method of 20" PMT to 3" PMT to measure the linearity of the 20" dynode and MCP PMTs in pulse mode with a waveform digitizer. The measurements show a good linear response of 20" PMTs to 1,000 photoelectrons (p.e.).

title: Photon production rate from Transverse-Longitudinal ( T − L T-L ) mesonic correlator on the lattice
creator: T. Ueding
description: Abstract Thermal photons from the QGP provide important information about the interaction among plasma constituents. The photon production rate from a thermally equilibrated system is proportional to the transverse spectral function ρ T ​ ( ω = | k → | , k → ) \rho_{T}(\omega=|\vec{k}|,\vec{k}) .

title: Theory of non-linear diffusion with a physical gapped mode
creator: Navid Abbasi, Matthias Kaminski, Omid Tavakol
description: Abstract In a system with one conserved charge the charge diffusion is modified by non-linear self-interactions within an effective field theory (EFT) of diffusive fluctuations. We include the slowest ultraviolet (UV) mode, constructing a UV-regulated EFT. The relaxation time of this UV mode is protected from renormalization, as supported by experimental data in a bad metal system.

title: Accelerating Barnes-Hut t-SNE Algorithm by Efficient Parallelization on Multi-Core CPUs
creator: Narendra Chaudhary, Alexander Pivovar, Pavel Yakovlev, Andrey Gorshkov, Sanchit Misra
description: Abstract . t-SNE remains one of the most popular embedding techniques for visualizing high-dimensional data. Most standard packages of t-SNE, such as scikit-learn, use the Barnes-Hut t-SNE (BH t-SNE) algorithm for large datasets. However, existing CPU implementations of this algorithm are inefficient.

title: Co-evolving morphology and control of soft robots using a single genome
creator: Fabio Tanaka, Claus Aranha
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fabio Tanaka, Claus Aranha. When simulating soft robots, both their morphology and their controllers play important roles in task performance. This paper introduces a new method to co-evolve these two components in the same process. We do that by using the hyperNEAT algorithm to generate two separate neural networks in one pass, one responsible for the design of the robot body structure and the other for the control of the robot.

title: Scaffolding Generation using a 3D Physarum Polycephalum Simulation
creator: Drew Ehrlich, Milad Hakimshafaei, Oskar Elek
description: Abstract In this demo, we present a novel technique for approximating topologically optimal scaffoldings for 3D printed objects using a Monte Carlo algorithm based on the foraging behavior of the Physarum polycephalum slime mold. As a case study, we have created a biologically inspired bicycle helmet using this technique that is designed to be effective in resisting impacts.

title: Group Actions on Product Systems
creator: Valentin Deaconu, Leonard Huang
description: Abstract . We introduce the concept of crossed product of a product system by a locally compact group. We prove that the crossed product of a row-finite and faithful product system by an amenable group is also a row-finite and faithful product system.

title: QED radiative corrections to electric dipole amplitudes in heavy atoms
creator: C. J. Fairhall, B. M. Roberts, J. S. M. Ginges
description: Abstract We use the radiative potential method to perform a detailed study of quantum electrodynamics (QED) radiative corrections to electric dipole (E1) transition amplitudes in heavy alkali-metal atoms Rb, Cs, Fr, and alkali-metal-like ions Sr + , Ba + , and Ra + .

title: Uncovering tau leptons-enriched semi-visible jets at the LHC Journal: Noname
creator: Hugues Beauchesne e1,addr1 ID, Cesare Cazzaniga e2,addr2 ID, Annapaola de Cosa e3,addr2 ID, Caterina Doglioni e4,addr3 ID, Tobias Fitschen e5,addr3 ID, Giovanni Grilli di Cortona e6,addr8,addr9 ID, Ziyuan Zhou e7,addr2,addr7 ID
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hugues Beauchesne e1,addr1 ID, Cesare Cazzaniga e2,addr2 ID, Annapaola de Cosa e3,addr2 ID, Caterina Doglioni e4,addr3 ID, Tobias Fitschen e5,addr3 ID, Giovanni Grilli di Cortona e6,addr8,addr9 ID, Ziyuan Zhou e7,addr2,addr7 ID. This Letter proposes a new signature for confining dark sectors at the Large Hadron Collider. Under the assumption of a QCD-like hidden sector, hadronic jets containing stable dark bound states could manifest in proton-proton collisions.

title: Role of the scalar f 0 ​ ( 980 ) f_{0}(980) in the process D s + → π + ​ π 0 ​ π 0 D_{s}^{+}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{0}\pi^{0}
creator: Han Zhang, Yun-He Lyu, Li-Juan Liu, En Wang
description: Abstract Based on the BESIII measurements on the reaction of D s + → π + ​ π 0 ​ π 0 D_{s}^{+}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{0}\pi^{0} , we investigate this process by considering the S S -wave pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar interaction within the unitary chiral approach, and the contributions from the intermediate resonances f 0 ​ ( 1370 ) f_{0}(1370) and f 2 ​ (

title: Explicit derivation of the chiral and (generic) helical edge states for the Kane-Mele model: Closed expressions for the wave function, dispersion relation, and spin rotation
creator: Fatemeh Rahmati, Mohsen Amini, Morteza Soltani, Mozhgan Sadeghizadeh
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fatemeh Rahmati, Mohsen Amini, Morteza Soltani, Mozhgan Sadeghizadeh. While one of the most important and intriguing features of the topological insulators is the presence of edge states, the closed-form expressions for the edge states of some famous topological models are still lacking. Here, we focus on the Kane-Mele model with and without Rashba spin-orbit coupling as a well-known model to describe a two-dimensional version of the ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} topological insulator to study the properties of its edge states analytically.

title: Hadronic vacuum polarization with C* boundary conditions
creator: Paola Tavella
description: Abstract We present a progress report on the calculation of the connected hadronic contribution to the muon g − 2 g-2 with C ⋆ boundary conditions. For that purpose we use a QCD gauge ensemble with 3+1 flavors and two QCD+QED gauge ensembles with 1+2+1 flavors of dynamical quarks generated by the RC ⋆ collaboration.

title: Scaling, saturation, and upper bounds in the failure of topologically interlocked structures
creator: Shai Feldfogel, Konstantinos Karapiperis, Jose Andrade, David S. Kammer
description: Abstract Topological Interlocking Structures (TIS) have been increasingly studied in the past two decades. However, some fundamental questions concerning the effects of Young’s modulus and the friction coefficient on the structural mechanics of the most common type of TIS application - centrally loaded slabs - are not yet clear.

title: Quantization dimensions for the bi-Lipschitz recurrent Iterated function systems
creator: Amit Priyadarshi, Mrinal K. Roychowdhury, Manuj Verma
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Amit Priyadarshi, Mrinal K. Roychowdhury, Manuj Verma. In this paper, the quantization dimensions of the Borel probability measures supported on the limit sets of the bi-Lipschitz recurrent iterated function systems under the strong open set condition in terms of the spectral radius have been estimated.

title: Weak convergence of Monge-Ampère measures on compact Hermitian manifolds
creator: Sławomir Kołodziej and Ngoc Cuong Nguyen
description: Abstract . We give a sufficient condition on a sequence of uniformly bounded ω \omega -plurisubharmonic functions, ω \omega being a Hermitian metric, for which the sequence of associated Monge-Ampère measures converges weakly. This criterion can be used to obtained a bounded ω \omega -plurisubharmonic solution to the Monge-Ampère equation. 1.

title: Elastic precursor effects during the Ba 1-x Sr x TiO 3 ferroelastic phase transitions
creator: Francesco Cordero, Francesco Trequattrini, Paulo Sergio da Silva Jr, Michel Venet, Oktay Aktas, Ekhard K. H. Salje
description: Abstract Elastic softening in the paraelastic phases of Ba 1-x Sr x TiO 3 is largest near the transition temperatures and decreases on heating smoothly over extended temperature ranges. Softening extends to the highest measured temperature(850 K) for Ba-rich compounds.

title: The influence of finite size particles on fluid velocity and transport though porous media
creator: M. Residori, S. Praetorius, P. de Anna, A. Voigt
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by M. Residori, S. Praetorius, P. de Anna, A. Voigt. Understanding the coupling between flow, hydrodynamic transport and dispersion of colloids of finite size in porous media is a long-standing challenge. This problem is relevant for a broad range of natural and engineered processes, including contaminant and colloidal transport, mixing of bio-chemical compounds, kinetics of reactions and groundwater bio-remediation, but also transport phenomena related to different systems like membranes, or blood flow.

title: Identify 46 New Open Clusters Candidates In Gaia EDR3 Using pyUPMASK and Random Forest Hybrid Method Journal: ApJS
creator: Huanbin Chi (gbsn迟焕斌), Shoulin Wei (gbsn卫守林), Feng Wang (gbsn王锋), Zhongmu Li (gbsn李忠木)
description: Abstract Open clusters (OCs) are regarded as tracers to understand stellar evolution theory and validate stellar models. In this study, we presented a robust approach to identifying OCs. A hybrid method of pyUPMASK and RF is first used to remove field stars and determine more reliable members.

title: Local spatial densities for composite spin-3/2 systems
creator: H. Alharazin, B.-D. Sun, E. Epelbaum, J. Gegelia, U.-G. Meißner
description: Abstract The definition of local spatial densities by using sharply localized one-particle states is applied to spin-3/2 systems. Matrix elements of the electromagnetic current and the energy-momentum tensor are considered and integral expressions of associated spatial distributions in terms of form factors are derived.

title: Bilinear maximal functions associated with degenerate surfaces
creator: Sanghyuk Lee and Kalachand Shuin
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sanghyuk Lee and Kalachand Shuin. We study L p × L q → L r L^{p}\times L^{q}\rightarrow L^{r} -boundedness of (sub)bilinear maximal functions associated with degenerate hypersurfaces. First, we obtain the maximal bound on the sharp range of exponents p , q , r p,q,r (except some border line cases) for the bilinear maximal functions given by the model surface { ( y , z ) ∈ ℝ n × ℝ n : | y | l 1 + | z | l 2

title: A hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method with characteristic variables for Helmholtz problems Published in Journal of Computational Physics (doi: 10.1016/j.jcp.2023.112459 ). Distributed under Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0 license.
creator: Axel Modave, Théophile Chaumont-Frelet
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Axel Modave, Théophile Chaumont-Frelet. A new hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method, named the CHDG method, is proposed for solving time-harmonic scalar wave propagation problems. This method relies on a standard discontinuous Galerkin scheme with upwind numerical fluxes and high-order polynomial bases. Auxiliary unknowns corresponding to characteristic variables are defined at the interface between the elements, and the physical fields are eliminated to obtain a reduced system. The reduced system can be written as a fixed-point problem that can be solved with stationary iterative schemes.

title: Constraining the Georgi-Machacek Model with a Light Higgs
creator: Amine Ahriche ID
description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the viability of a light Higgs ( η \eta ) scenario in the Georgi-Machacek (GM) model, where we consider all theoretical and experimental constraints such as the perturbativity, vacuum stability, unitarity, electroweak precision tests, the Higgs di-photon and undetermined decays and the Higgs total decay width.

title: A motorized rotation mount for fast and reproducible optical polarization control
creator: Adarsh P. Raghuram, Jonathan M. Mortlock, Sarah L. Bromley, Simon L. Cornish
description: Abstract We present a simple motorised rotation mount for a half-wave plate that can be used to rapidly change the polarization of light. We use the device to switch a high power laser beam between different optical dipole traps in an ultracold atom experiment.

title: Deformable Surface Reconstruction via Riemannian Metric Preservation
creator: Oriol Barbany Adrià Colomé Carme Torras[1ex] Institut de Robòtica i Informàtica Industrial (CSIC-UPC), Barcelona, Spain
description: Abstract Estimating the pose of an object from a monocular image is an inverse problem fundamental in computer vision. The ill-posed nature of this problem requires incorporating deformation priors to solve it. In practice, many materials do not perceptibly shrink or extend when manipulated, constituting a powerful and well-known prior. Mathematically, this translates to the preservation of the Riemannian metric.

title: Motion, Unit Dual Quaternion and Motion Optimization
creator: Liqun Qi
description: Abstract We introduce motions as real six-dimensional vectors. A motion means a rotation and a translation. We define a motion operator which maps unit dual quaternions to motions, and a UDQ operator which maps motions to unit dual quaternions. By these operators, we present the formulation of motion optimization, which is actually a real unconstrained optimization formulation.

title: Local well-posedness of Kolmogorov’s two-equation model of turbulence in fractional Sobolev Spaces
creator: Przemysław Kosewski
description: Abstract We study Kolmogorov’s two-equation model of turbulence on d − d- dimensional torus. First, the local existence of the solution with the initial data from non-homogeneous fractional Sobolev spaces (Bessel potential spaces) H s H^{s} with s > d 2 s>\frac{d}{2} is proven using energy methods.

title: Transmitter Selection for Secrecy in Frequency-Selective Fading with Multiple Eavesdroppers and Wireless Backhaul Links
creator: Shashi Bhushan Kotwal, Chinmoy Kundu, Sudhakar Modem, Mark F. Flanagan
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shashi Bhushan Kotwal, Chinmoy Kundu, Sudhakar Modem, Mark F. Flanagan. This paper investigates the secrecy performance of sub-optimal transmitter selection (SS) and optimal selection (OS) schemes in a system comprising multiple transmitters, multiple eavesdroppers, and a single destination in frequency-selective fading channels with single carrier cyclic prefix modulation. Considering unreliable backhaul links between the access point and the transmitters, we analyze secrecy performance in two scenarios: when backhaul activity knowledge is available (KA) and when backhaul activity knowledge is unavailable (KU).

title: Minimal Entropy Conditions for Scalar Conservation Laws with General Convex Fluxes Thanks: Gaowei Cao was supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China No.11701551 and No.11971024, and the China Scholarship Council No.202004910200 Thanks: Gui-Qiang G. Chen was supported in pa
creator: Gaowei Cao, Gui-Qiang G. Chen †
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gaowei Cao, Gui-Qiang G. Chen †. We are concerned with the minimal entropy conditions for one-dimensional scalar conservation laws with general convex flux functions. For such scalar conservation laws, we prove that a single entropy-entropy flux pair ( η ⁡ ( u ) , q ⁡ ( u ) ) (\eta(u),q(u)) with η ⁡ ( u ) \eta(u) of strict convexity is sufficient to single out an entropy solution from a broad class of weak solutions in L loc ∞ L^{\infty}_{\rm loc} that satisfy

title: Locally conformal SKT almost abelian Lie algebras
creator: Louis-Brahim Beaufort, Anna Fino
description: Abstract . A locally conformal SKT (shortly LCSKT) structure is a Hermitian structure ( J , g ) (J,g) whose Bismut torsion 3-form H H satisfies the condition d ​ H = α ∧ H dH=\alpha\wedge H , for some closed non-zero 1-form α \alpha .

title: Curved domain-wall fermion and its anomaly inflow
creator: Shoto Aoki, Hidenori Fukaya
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shoto Aoki, Hidenori Fukaya. We investigate the effect of U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) gauge field on lattice fermion systems with a curved domain-wall mass term. In the same way as the conventional flat domain-wall fermion, the chiral edge modes appear localized at the wall, whose Dirac operator contains the induced gravitational potential as well as the U ⁡ ( 1 ) U(1) vector potential.

title: Reviewing Best Practices in Online Conferencing
creator: Simone Ferlin, Oliver Hohlfeld, Vaibhav Bajpai
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Simone Ferlin, Oliver Hohlfeld, Vaibhav Bajpai. The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the usual ways the networking research community operates. This article reviews experiences organising and participating in virtual conferences during the COVID-19 pandemic between 2020-2021.

title: An estimate of the centroid Banach-Mazur distance between planar convex bodies
description: Abstract Marek Lassak Abstract. We consider the variant of the Banach-Mazur distance \delta_{BM}^{\rm cen}(C,D) of two convex bodies C,D of E^{d} with the additional requirement that the centroids of them coincide. We prove that \delta_{BM}^{\rm cen}(C,D)\leq\frac{69}{17} for every convex bodies C,D of E^{2} .

title: Polyakov’s confinement mechanism for generalized Maxwell theory Preprint: PUPT- 2636
creator: Matthew Heydeman, a,b Christian B. Jepsen, c Ziming Ji, d,e, Amos Yarom f
description: Abstract We study fractional-derivative Maxwell theory, as appears in effective descriptions of, for example, large N f N_{f} QED 3 , graphene, and some types of surface defects. We argue that when the theory is UV completed on a lattice, monopole condensation leads to a confining phase via the Polyakov confinement mechanism.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Generative Adversarial Network for High Resolution Image Generation
creator: Shu Lok Tsang, Maxwell T. West, Sarah M. Erfani, Muhammad Usman
description: Abstract Quantum machine learning (QML) has received increasing attention due to its potential to outperform classical machine learning methods in problems pertaining classification and identification tasks. A subclass of QML methods is quantum generative adversarial networks (QGANs) which have been studied as a quantum counterpart of classical GANs widely used in image manipulation and generation tasks.

title: Characterization of Quantumness of non-Gaussian states under the influence of Gaussian channel
creator: Ramniwas Meena, Subhashish Banerjee
description: Abstract The impact of a noisy Gaussian channel on a wide range of non-Gaussian input states is studied in this work. The nonclassical nature of the states, both input and output, is developed by studying the corresponding photon statistics and quasi-probability distributions.

title: Counterexamples in self-testing
creator: Laura Mančinska, Simon Schmidt
description: Abstract In the recent years self-testing has grown into a rich and active area of study with applications ranging from practical verification of quantum devices to deep complexity theoretic results. Self-testing allows a classical verifier to deduce which quantum measurements and on what state are used, for example, by provers Alice and Bob in a nonlocal game.

title: Graph-Based Specification and Automated Construction of ILP Problems
creator: Sebastian Ehmes Maximilian Kratz Andy Schürr
description: Abstract In the MDSE ( MDSE ) community, the combination of techniques operating on graph-based models (e.g., PM ( PM ) and GT ( GT )) and ILP ( ILP ) is a common occurrence, since ILP solvers offer a powerful approach to solve linear optimization problems and help to enforce global constraints while delivering optimal solutions.

title: Reducing the frequency of the Higgs mode in a helical superconductor coupled to an LC-circuit
creator: Yao Lu, Stefan Ilić, Risto Ojajärvi, Tero T. Heikkilä, F. Sebastian Bergeret
description: Abstract We show that the amplitude, or Higgs mode of a superconductor with strong spin-orbit coupling and an exchange field, couples linearly to the electromagnetic field. Furthermore, by coupling such a superconductor to an LC resonator, we demonstrate that the Higgs resonance becomes a regular mode at frequencies smaller than the quasiparticle energy threshold 2 ​ Δ 2\Delta .

title: Soft and Collinear Limits in 𝒩 = 8 \mathcal{N}=8 Supergravity using Double Copy Formalism
creator: Nabamita Banerjee, Tabasum Rahnuma, and Ranveer Kumar Singh
description: Abstract It is known that 𝒩 = 8 \mathcal{N}=8 supergravity is dual to 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 super Yang-Mills (SYM) via the double copy relation. Using the explicit relation between scattering amplitudes in the two theories, we calculate the soft and collinear limits in 𝒩 = 8 \mathcal{N}=8 supergravity from know results in 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SYM.

title: Boosted top tagging and its interpretation using Shapley values
creator: Biplob Bhattacherjee, Camellia Bose, Amit Chakraborty, and Rhitaja Sengupta
description: Abstract Top tagging has emerged as a fast-evolving subject due to the top quark’s significant role in probing physics beyond the standard model. For the reconstruction of top jets, machine learning models have shown a substantial improvement in the classification performance compared to the previous methods.

title: Performance enhancement of surface codes via recursive MWPM decoding
creator: Antonio deMarti iOlius, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Patricio Fuentes, Pedro M. Crespo
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Antonio deMarti iOlius, Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Patricio Fuentes, Pedro M. Crespo. The minimum weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoder is the standard decoding strategy for quantum surface codes. However, it suffers a harsh decrease in performance when subjected to biased or non-identical quantum noise. In this work, we modify the conventional MWPM decoder so that it considers the biases, the non-uniformities and the relationship between X X , Y Y and Z Z errors of the constituent qubits of a given surface code.

title: Towards Mechanised Proofs inDouble-Pushout Graph Transformation
creator: Robert Söldner Detlef Plump
description: Abstract We formalise the basics of the double-pushout approach to graph transformation in the proof assistant Isabelle/HOL and provide associated machine-checked proofs. Specifically, we formalise graphs, graph morphisms and rules, and a definition of direct derivations based on deletion and gluing. We then formalise graph pushouts and prove with Isabelle’s help that both deletions and gluings are pushouts.

title: Anharmonic effects on the reflectivity of CaS and MgS: A first-principles based study
creator: Artem Chmeruk, Maribel Núñez-Valdez
description: Abstract We employ systematic calculations based on density functional theory to model the reflectivity of CaS and MgS in the infrared region. We show that in addition to the modeling using the harmonic approximation, an accurate spectral description requires the inclusion of anharmonic effects.

title: Low intensity saturation of an ISB transition by a mid-IR quantum cascade laser
creator: Mathieu Jeannin, Eduardo Cosentino, Stefano Pirotta, Mario Malerba, Giorgio Biasiol, Jean-Michel Manceau, Raffaele Colombelli
description: Abstract We demonstrate that absorption saturation of a mid-infrared intersubband transition can be engineered to occur at moderate light intensities of the order of 10-20 kW.cm -2 and at room temperature. The structure consists of an array of metal-semiconductor-metal patches hosting a judiciously designed 253 nm thick GaAs/AlGaAs semiconductor heterostructure.

title: Less Interaction with forward models in Langevin Dynamics
creator: Martin Eigel, Robert Gruhlke, David Sommer
description: Abstract Ensemble methods have become ubiquitous for the solution of Bayesian inference problems. State-of-the-art Langevin samplers such as the Ensemble Kalman Sampler (EKS), Affine Invariant Langevin Dynamics (ALDI) or its extension using weighted covariance estimates rely on successive evaluations of the forward model or its gradient.

title: Quantum Coherent Control of a Single Molecular-Polariton Rotation
creator: Li-Bao Fan, Chuan-Cun Shu, Daoyi Dong, Jun He, Niels E. Henriksen, Franco Nori
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Li-Bao Fan, Chuan-Cun Shu, Daoyi Dong, Jun He, Niels E. Henriksen, Franco Nori. We present a combined analytical and numerical study for coherent terahertz control of a single molecular polariton, formed by strongly coupling two rotational states of a molecule with a single-mode cavity. Compared to the bare molecules driven by a single terahertz pulse, the presence of a cavity strongly modifies the post-pulse orientation of the polariton, making it difficult to obtain its maximal degree of orientation.

title: Improving metallicity estimates for very metal-poor stars in the Gaia DR3 GSP-Spec catalog
creator: Tadafumi Matsuno, Else Starkenburg, Eduardo Balbinot, Amina Helmi
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tadafumi Matsuno, Else Starkenburg, Eduardo Balbinot, Amina Helmi. In the latest Gaia data release (DR3), the GSP-Spec module has provided stellar parameters and chemical abundances measured from the RVS spectra alone. However, the GSP-Spec parameters, including metallicity, for very metal-poor stars (VMP stars; [ Fe / H ] < − 2 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]<-2 ) suffer from parameter degeneracy due to a lack of information in their spectra, and hence have large measurement uncertainty and systematic offset.

title: On the growth rates of polyregular functions Note: This is the author’s version of a LICS 2023 paper. CCS: Theory of computation Regular languages
creator: Mikołaj Bojańczyk (University of Warsaw)
description: Abstract . We consider polyregular functions, which are certain string-to-string functions that have polynomial output size. We prove that a polyregular function has output size 𝒪 ⁡ ( n k ) {\mathcal{O}}(n^{k}) if and only if it can be defined by an mso interpretation of dimension k k , i.e.

title: Evaluation for Change
creator: Rishi Bommasani
description: Abstract Evaluation is the central means for assessing, understanding, and communicating about NLP models. In this position paper, we argue evaluation should be more than that: it is a force for driving change, carrying a sociological and political character beyond its technical dimensions.

title: Polarized tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy at liquid He temperature in ultrahigh vacuum using an off-axis parabolic mirror
creator: L. Peis, G. He, D. Jost, G. Rager, R. Hackl
description: Abstract Tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) combines inelastic light scattering well below the diffraction limit down to the nanometer range and scanning probe microscopy and, possibly, spectroscopy. In this way, topographic and spectroscopic as well as single- and two-particle information may simultaneously be collected. While single molecules can now be studied successfully, bulk solids are still not meaningfully accessible.

title: Time and Space Measures for a Complete Graph Computation Model
creator: Brian Courtehoute and Detlef Plump
description: Abstract We present a computation model based on a subclass of GP 2 graph programs which can simulate any off-line Turing machine of space complexity O ⁡ ( s ⁡ ( n ) ​ log ⁡ s ​ ( n ) ) \mathrm{O}(s(n)\log s(n)) in space O ⁡ ( s ⁡ ( n ) ) \mathrm{O}(s(n)) .

title: Bounding the multiplicities of eigenvalues of graph matrices in terms of circuit rank using a new approach
creator: Ahmet Batal
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ahmet Batal. Let G G be a simple undirected graph, θ ⁡ ( G ) \theta(G) be the circuit rank of G G , η M ​ ( G ) \eta_{M}(G) and m M ​ ( G , λ ) m_{M}(G,\lambda) be the nullity and the multiplicity of eigenvalue λ \lambda of a graph matrix M ⁡ ( G ) M(G) , respectively.

title: Metadynamics Surfing on Topology Barriers in the Schwinger Model
creator: Lukas Varnhorst
description: Abstract Topological freezing is a well known problem in lattice simulations: with shrinking lattice spacing a transition between topological sectors becomes increasingly improbable, leading to a problematic increase of the autocorrelation time regarding several observables. We present our investigation of metadynamics as a solution for topological freezing in the Schwinger model.

title: Integrability of two-species partially asymmetric exclusion processes
creator: Ivan Lobaskin, Martin R Evans, Kirone Mallick
description: Abstract We work towards the classification of all one-dimensional exclusion processes with two species of particles that can be solved by a nested coordinate Bethe Ansatz. Using the Yang-Baxter equations, we obtain conditions on the model parameters that ensure that the underlying system is integrable. Three classes of integrable models are thus found.

title: Trustworthy Social Bias Measurement
creator: Rishi Bommasani, Percy Liang
description: Abstract How do we design measures of social bias that we trust ? While prior work has introduced several measures, no measure has gained widespread trust: instead, mounting evidence argues we should distrust these measures. In this work, we design bias measures that warrant trust based on the cross-disciplinary theory of measurement modeling.

title: Some reflections on the test-negative design
creator: Ronald Meester, Jan Bonte
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ronald Meester, Jan Bonte. We discuss some philosophical, methodological and practical problems concerning the use of the test-negative design for COVID-19 vaccines. These problems limit the use of this design considerably. The test-negative design was developed as a method to estimate influenza vaccine effectiveness, but has more recently also been used in the context of COVID-19 vaccines [ 1 , 3 , 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 ] .

title: DuAT: Dual-Aggregation Transformer Network for Medical Image Segmentation
creator: Feilong Tang, Qiming Huang, Jinfeng Wang, Xianxu Hou, Jionglong Su 🖂, Jingxin Liu 🖂
description: Abstract Transformer-based models have been widely demonstrated to be successful in computer vision tasks by modelling long-range dependencies and capturing global representations. However, they are often dominated by features of large patterns leading to the loss of local details (e.g., boundaries and small objects), which are critical in medical image segmentation.

title: Exact analytical vacuum solutions of R n R^{n} -gravity model depending on two variables
creator: Maria Shubina
description: Abstract In this paper we consider the metric power-law f ⁡ ( R ) ∼ R n f(R)\sim R^{n} -gravity model for the four-dimensional metric tensor depending on two coordinates. We obtain exact analytical vacuum solutions for different values of n n .

title: Multi muon/anti-muon signals via productions of gauge and scalar bosons in a U ​ ( 1 ) L μ − L τ U(1)_{L_{\mu}-L_{\tau}} model at muonic colliders Preprint: UME-PP-024
creator: Arindam Das, Takaaki Nomura, Takashi Shimomura
description: Abstract We discuss the discovery potential of a promising signals, 3 × μ + ​ μ − 3\times\mu^{+}\mu^{-} at a μ + ​ μ − \mu^{+}\mu^{-} collider and μ + ​ μ + ​ μ + ​ μ + ​ μ − ​ μ − \mu^{+}\mu^{+}\mu^{+}\mu^{+}\mu^{-}\mu^{-} at a μ + ​ μ + \mu^{+}\mu^{+} collider, that are obtained via production

title: The s s -weak order and s s -permutahedra I: combinatorics and lattice structure Thanks: This project was supported by the ANR-FWF International Cooperation Project PAGCAP, funded by the ANR Project ANR-21-CE48-0020 and the FWF Project I 5788. Cesar Ceballos was also supported by the Austrian Scienc
creator: Cesar Ceballos ⋄, Viviane Pons ⋆
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Cesar Ceballos ⋄, Viviane Pons ⋆. This is the first contribution of a sequence of papers introducing the notions of s s -weak order and s s -permutahedra, certain discrete objects that are indexed by a sequence of non-negative integers s s . In this first paper, we concentrate purely on the combinatorics and lattice structure of the s s -weak order, a partial order on certain decreasing trees which generalizes the classical weak order on permutations.

title: Active SLAM: A Review on Last Decade
creator: Muhammad Farhan Ahmed, Khayyam Masood, Vincent Fremont *, Isabelle Fantoni
description: Abstract This article presents a comprehensive review of the Active Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (A-SLAM) research conducted over the past decade. It explores the formulation, applications, and methodologies employed in A-SLAM, particularly in trajectory generation and control-action selection, drawing on concepts from Information Theory (IT) and the Theory of Optimal Experimental Design (TOED).

title: Scene-aware Egocentric 3D Human Pose Estimation
creator: Jian Wang Diogo Luvizon Weipeng Xu Lingjie Liu, Kripasindhu Sarkar Christian Theobalt
description: Abstract Egocentric 3D human pose estimation with a single head-mounted fisheye camera has recently attracted attention due to its numerous applications in virtual and augmented reality. Existing methods still struggle in challenging poses where the human body is highly occluded or is closely interacting with the scene.

title: Exploring Student Engagement and Outcomes: Experiences from Three Cycles of an Undergraduate Module
creator: Robert D. Macredie, Martin Shepperd, Tommaso Turchi, Terry Young
description: Abstract Many studies in educational data mining address specific learner groups, such as first-in-family to attend Higher Education, or focus on differences in characteristics such as gender or ethnicity, with the aim of predicting performance and designing interventions to improve outcomes.

title: Weighted projections of alternating sign matrices: Latin-like squares and the ASM polytope
creator: Cian O’Brien obrien.cian@outlook.com
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Cian O’Brien obrien.cian@outlook.com. The weighted projection of an alternating sign matrix (ASM) was introduced by Brualdi and Dahl (2018) as a step towards characterising a generalisation of Latin squares they introduced using alternating sign hypermatrices. If z n = ( n , … , 2 , 1 ) z_{n}=(n,\dots,2,1) , then the weighted projection of an ASM A A is equal to z n T ​ A z_{n}^{T}A .

title: Smooth Sailing: Improving Active Learning for Pre-trained Language Models with Representation Smoothness Analysis
creator: Josip Jukić, Jan Šnajder
description: Abstract Developed to alleviate prohibitive labeling costs, active learning (AL) methods aim to reduce label complexity in supervised learning. While recent work has demonstrated the benefit of using AL in combination with large pre-trained language models (PLMs), it has often overlooked the practical challenges that hinder the effectiveness of AL.

title: Variational Quantum Soft Actor-Critic for Robotic Arm Control
creator: Alberto Acuto, Paola Barillà, Ludovico Bozzolo, Matteo Conterno, Mattia Pavese, Antonio Policicchio
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alberto Acuto, Paola Barillà, Ludovico Bozzolo, Matteo Conterno, Mattia Pavese, Antonio Policicchio. Abstract Deep Reinforcement Learning is emerging as a promising approach for the continuous control task of robotic arm movement. However, the challenges of learning robust and versatile control capabilities are still far from being resolved for real-world applications, mainly because of two common issues of this learning paradigm: the exploration strategy and the slow learning speed, sometimes known as “the curse of dimensionality”.

title: Geometric genuine multipartite entanglement for four-qubit systems
creator: Ansh Mishra 1, Soumik Mahanti ∗2,3, Abhinash Kumar Roy 4, Prasanta K. Panigrahi 2
description: Abstract Xie and Eberly introduced a genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) measure ‘concurrence fill’( Phys. Rev. Lett., 127 , 040403 (2021)) for three-party systems. It is defined as the area of a triangle whose side lengths represent squared concurrence in each bi-partition.

title: Efficient wave type fingerprinting and filtering by six-component polarization analysis
creator: David Sollberger 1, Nicholas Bradley 1,2, Pascal Edme 1, Johan O. A. Robertsson 1 1 Institute of Geophysics, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland 2 Now at: Centre for Geophysical Forecasting, NTNU, Trondheim, Norway
description: Abstract \pagerange Efficient wave type fingerprinting and filtering by six-component polarization analysis – B keywords Rotational Seismology, Polarization Analysis, Signal Processing, Machine Learning. {summary} We present a technique to automatically classify the wave type of seismic phases that are recorded on a single six-component recording station (measuring both three components of translational and rotational ground motion) at the earth’s surface.

title: Spin-phonon decoherence in solid-state paramagnetic defects from first principles
creator: Sourav Mondal, Alessandro Lunghi
description: Abstract Paramagnetic defects in diamond and hexagonal boron nitride possess a unique combination of spin and optical properties that make them prototypical solid-state qubits. Despite the coherence of these spin qubits being critically limited by spin-phonon relaxation, a full understanding of this process is not yet available.

title: GOOD: Exploring Geometric Cues for Detecting Objects in an Open World
creator: Haiwen Huang Andreas Geiger Dan Zhang
description: Abstract We address the task of open-world class-agnostic object detection, i.e., detecting every object in an image by learning from a limited number of base object classes. State-of-the-art RGB-based models suffer from overfitting the training classes and often fail at detecting novel-looking objects.

title: Concentration of Equilibria and Relative Instability in Disordered Non-Relaxational Dynamics
creator: Pax Kivimae
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Pax Kivimae. We consider a system of random autonomous ODEs introduced by Cugliandolo et al. [ 1 ] , which serves as a non-relaxational analog of the gradient flow for the spherical p p -spin model. The asymptotics for the expected number of equilibria in this model was recently computed by Fyodorov [ 2 ] in the high-dimensional limit, followed a similar computation for the expected number of stable equilibria by Garcia [ 3 ] .

title: Spectral analysis of a family of nonsymmetric fractional elliptic operators Journal: Journal for review

description: Abstract In this work, we investigate the spectral problem { 𝒟 a + α ​ 𝒟 b − β ​ u = λ ​ u , x ∈ ( a , b ) u ( a ) = u ( b ) = 0 , 1 < α + β < 2 , \begin{cases}{\mathcal{D}_{a+}^{\alpha}}{\mathcal{D}_{b-}^{\beta}}u=\lambda u,\quad x\in(a,b)\\ u(a)=u(b)=0,1<\alpha+\beta<2,\end{cases} where the operators

title: Extraction of spin-averaged rovibrational transition frequencies in HD + \text{HD}^{+} for the determination of fundamental constants
creator: Jean-Philippe Karr a,b and Jeroen C. J. Koelemeij c
description: Abstract We present a comprehensive analysis of all currently available high-accuracy frequency measurements of rotational and rovibrational transitions in the hydrogen molecular ion HD + \text{HD}^{+} . Our analysis utilises the theoretically calculated hyperfine structure to extract the values of three spin-averaged transition frequencies through a global linear least-squares adjustment that takes into account theory-induced correlations between the different transitions.

title: Scalar product and distance in barycentric coordinates
creator: Vladimir Zolotov
description: Abstract . We give a formula for the scalar product and the distance in generalized barycentric coordinates for Euclidean and Pseudo-Euclidean spaces. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 51F99 1. Difference from MO post There is a MathOverflow post [ 5 ] giving the same formula.

title: GeoCode: Interpretable Shape Programs
creator: Ofek Pearl 1,2 Itai Lang 2 Yuhua Hu 2 Raymond A. Yeh 3 Rana Hanocka 2 1 Tel Aviv University 2 University of Chicago 3 Purdue University ofekpearl@mail.tau.ac.il {itailang, katehu, ranahanocka}@uchicago.edu rayyeh@purdue.edu, O. Pearl 1,2 I. Lang 2 Y. Hu 2 R. A. Yeh 3 R. Hanocka 2 1 Tel Aviv Universi
description: Abstract The task of crafting procedural programs capable of generating structurally valid 3D shapes easily and intuitively remains an elusive goal in computer vision and graphics. Within the graphics community, generating procedural 3D models has shifted to using node graph systems. They allow the artist to create complex shapes and animations through visual programming.

title: A topological analysis of cointegrated data: a Z24 Bridge case study
creator: T. Gowdridge, E.J. Cross, N. Dervilis, K. Worden
description: Abstract The paper studies the topological changes from before and after cointegration, for the natural frequencies of the Z24 Bridge. The second natural frequency is known to be nonlinear in temperature, and this will serve as the main focal point of this work.

title: Response to Moffat’s Comment on “Towards Meaningful Statements in IR Evaluation: Mapping Evaluation Measures to Interval Scales”
creator: Marco Ferrante, Nicola Ferro, Norbert Fuhr
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Marco Ferrante, Nicola Ferro, Norbert Fuhr. Moffat 2022 recently commented on our previous work published in the IEEE Access journal. Our work focused on how laying the foundations of our evaluation methodology into the representational theory of measurement can improve our knowledge and understanding of the evaluation measures we daily use in IR ( IR ) and how it can shed light on the different types of scales adopted by our evaluation measures; we also provided evidence, through extensive experimentation, on the impact and

title: Toward a Classification of Conformal Hypersurface Invariants
creator: Samuel Blitz ♭
description: Abstract . Hypersurfaces embedded in conformal manifolds appear frequently as boundary data in boundary-value problems in cosmology and string theory. Viewed as the non-null conformal infinity of a spacetime, we consider hypersurfaces embedded in a Riemannian (or Lorentzian) conformal manifold.

title: Predicting Companies’ ESG Ratings from News Articles Using Multivariate Timeseries Analysis CCS: Information systems Content analysis and feature selection
creator: Tanja Aue, Adam Jatowt, Michael Färber
description: Abstract . Environmental, social and governance (ESG) engagement of companies moved into the focus of public attention over recent years. With the requirements of compulsory reporting being implemented and investors incorporating sustainability in their investment decisions, the demand for a transparent and reliable ESG ratings is increasing.

title: Light Higgs boson in the NMSSM confronted with the CMS diphoton and ditau excesses Thanks: supported by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NNSFC) under grant Nos. 12275066, 11605123, 11547103, and 12074295.
creator: Weichao Li 1 Haoxue Qiao 1;1) Jingya Zhu 2;2)
description: Abstract In 2018, the CMS collaboration reported a di-photon excess around 95.3 GeV with a local significance of 2.8 σ \sigma . Interestingly, the CMS collaboration also reported a di-tau excess recently at 95 ∼ 100 ​ GeV 95\sim 100\ \mathrm{GeV} with a local significance of 2.6 ∼ 3.1 ​ σ 2.6\sim 3.1~\sigma .

title: A Self-Adjusting Fusion Representation Learning Model for Unaligned Text-Audio Sequences
creator: Kaicheng Yang, Ruxuan Zhang, Hua Xu, Kai Gao
description: Abstract Inter-modal interaction plays an indispensable role in multimodal sentiment analysis. Due to different modalities sequences are usually non-alignment, how to integrate relevant information of each modality to learn fusion representations has been one of the central challenges in multimodal learning.

title: Parameterizing Path Partitions
creator: Henning Fernau, Florent Foucaud, Kevin Mann, Utkarsh Padariya, Rajath Rao K.N
description: Abstract We study the algorithmic complexity of partitioning the vertex set of a given (di)graph into a small number of paths. The Path Partition problem ( PP ) has been studied extensively, as it includes Hamiltonian Path as a special case.

title: Long bet will lose: demystifying seemingly fair gambling via two-armed Futurity bandit
creator: Zengjing Chen, Huaijin Liang, Wei Wang, Xiaodong Yan
description: Abstract No matter how much some gamblers occasionally win, as long as they continue to gamble, sooner or later they will loss more to the casino, which is the so-called “long bet will lose”. Our results demonstrate the counter-intuitive phenomena that gamblers involve “long bet will lose” but casinos always advertise their unprofitable circumstances.

title: Robust Meta-Representation Learning via Global Label Inference and Classification
creator: Ruohan Wang, John Isak Texas Falk, Massimiliano Pontil, and Carlo Ciliberto
description: Abstract Few-shot learning (FSL) is a central problem in meta-learning, where learners must efficiently learn from few labeled examples. Within FSL, feature pre-training has become a popular strategy to significantly improve generalization performance. However, the contribution of pre-training to generalization performance is often overlooked and understudied, with limited theoretical understanding.

title: A Palm Space Approach to Non-Linear Hawkes Processes Thanks: 1 Supported by PhD grant of École Normale Supérieure, ENS-PSL
creator: Philippe Robert, Gaëtan Vignoud
description: Abstract . A Hawkes process on ℝ \mathbb{R} is a point process whose intensity function at time t t is a functional of its past activity before time t t . It is defined by its activation function Φ \Phi and its memory function h h .

title: Anchored heat kernel upper bounds on graphs with unbounded geometry and anti-trees
creator: Matthias Keller, Christian Rose
description: Abstract We derive Gaussian heat kernel bounds on graphs with respect to a fixed origin for large times under the assumption of a Sobolev inequality and volume doubling on large balls. The upper bound from our previous work [ KR22 ] is affected by a new correction term measuring the distance to the origin.

title: A literature review on different types of empirically evaluated bug localization approaches
creator: F.H. Zamfirov
description: Abstract I Introduction Today, software systems have a significant role in various domains among which are healthcare, entertainment, transport and logistics, and many more. It is only natural that with this increasing dependency on software, the number of software systems increases. Additionally, these systems become more and more complex.

title: S-Graphs+ : Real-time Localization and Mapping leveraging Hierarchical Representations
creator: Hriday Bavle, Jose Luis Sanchez-Lopez, Muhammad Shaheer, Javier Civera, Holger Voos
description: Abstract In this paper, we present an evolved version of Situational Graphs, which jointly models in a single optimizable factor graph (1) a pose graph, as a set of robot keyframes comprising associated measurements and robot poses, and (2) a 3D scene graph, as a high-level representation of the environment that encodes its different geometric elements with semantic attributes and

title: Quantum Effects of Impurities and Lattice Defects in Topological Semimetals
creator: João Pedro dos Santos Pires
description: Abstract \subject Thesis Submitted in Fulfilment of the Requirements for the Degree of PHILOSOPHIÆ DOCTOR in PHYSICS \publishers \publishers \publishers \publishers Universidade do Porto Departamento de Física e Astronomia, Faculdade de Ciências Laboratory of Physics for Materials and Emergent Technologies LaPMET \lowertitleback Chair: Prof. João M. Borregana Lopes dos Santos (Universidade do Porto, Portugal) Supervisors: Prof.

title: Weak error analysis for a nonlinear SPDE approximation of the Dean-Kawasaki equation
creator: Helena Kremp, Ana Djurdjevac, Helena Kremp, Nicolas Perkowski
description: Abstract We consider a nonlinear SPDE approximation of the Dean-Kawasaki equation for independent particles. Our approximation satisfies the physical constraints of the particle system, i.e. its solution is a probability measure for all times (preservation of positivity and mass conservation).

title: Broken Symmetries in Microfluidic Pillar Arrays are Reflected in a Flowing DNA Solution across Multiple Length Scales
creator: Jason P. Beech*, Oskar E. Ström*, Jonas O. Tegenfeldt†
description: Abstract Unlike Newtonian fluids, viscoelastic fluids may break time-reversal symmetry at low Reynolds numbers resulting in elastic turbulence. Furthermore, under some conditions, instead of the chaotic turbulence, large-scale regular waves form, as has been shown for DNA flowing in microfluidic pillar arrays.

title: Training Integer-Only Deep Recurrent Neural Networks
creator: Vahid Partovi Nia, Eyyüb Sari, Vanessa Courville, Masoud Asgharian
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vahid Partovi Nia, Eyyüb Sari, Vanessa Courville, Masoud Asgharian. Recurrent neural networks (RNN) are the backbone of many text and speech applications. These architectures are typically made up of several computationally complex components such as; non-linear activation functions, normalization, bi-directional dependence and attention. In order to maintain good accuracy, these components are frequently run using full-precision floating-point computation, making them slow, inefficient and difficult to deploy on edge devices.

title: Normalized Contrastive Learning for Text-Video Retrieval
creator: Yookoon Park, Mahmoud Azab, Bo Xiong, Seungwhan Moon, Florian Metze, Gourab Kundu, Kirmani Ahmed
description: Abstract Cross-modal contrastive learning has led the recent advances in multimodal retrieval with its simplicity and effectiveness. In this work, however, we reveal that cross-modal contrastive learning suffers from incorrect normalization of the sum retrieval probabilities of each text or video instance.

title: Mind the Retrosynthesis Gap: Bridging the divide between Single-step and Multi-step Retrosynthesis Prediction
creator: Alan Kai HassenLeiden Institute of Advanced Computer ScienceLeiden UniversityLeiden, The Netherlands a.k.hassen@liacs.leidenuniv.nl, Paula Torren-PeraireInstitute of Structural BiologyMolecular Targets and Therapeutics CenterHelmholtz Zentrum MünchenNeuherberg, Germany paula.torren@helmholtz-munich.
description: Abstract Retrosynthesis is the task of breaking down a chemical compound recursively step-by-step into molecular precursors until a set of commercially available molecules is found. Consequently, the goal is to provide a valid synthesis route for a molecule. As more single-step models develop, we see increasing accuracy in the prediction of molecular disconnections, potentially improving the creation of synthetic paths.

title: On the REM approximation of TAP free energies. Thanks: This work has been supported by a DFG research grant, contract number 2337/1-1. NK wishes to express his gratitude to Anton Bovier for constant support and interest in this line of research.
creator: Nicola Kistler, Marius A. Schmidt, Giulia Sebastiani
description: Abstract . The free energy of TAP-solutions for the SK-model of mean field spin glasses can be expressed as a nonlinear functional of local terms: we exploit this feature in order to contrive abstract REM-like models which we then solve by a classical large deviations treatment.

title: EuclidNets: An Alternative Operation for Efficient Inference of Deep Learning Models
creator: Xinlin Li, Mariana Parazeres, Adam Oberman, Alireza Ghaffari, Masoud Asgharian, Vahid Partovi Nia
description: Abstract With the advent of deep learning application on edge devices, researchers actively try to optimize their deployments on low-power and restricted memory devices. There are established compression method such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search that leverage commodity hardware. Apart from conventional compression algorithms, one may redesign the operations of deep learning models that lead to more efficient implementation.

title: A Mutation-based Text Generation for Adversarial Machine Learning Applications
creator: Jesus Guerrero, Gongbo Liang, Izzat Alsmadi
description: Abstract Many natural language related applications involve text generation, created by humans or machines. While in many of those applications machines support humans, yet in few others, (e.g. adversarial machine learning, social bots and trolls) machines try to impersonate humans. In this scope, we proposed and evaluated several mutation-based text generation approaches.

title: First-order sentences in random groups II: ∀ ∃ \forall\exists -sentences.
creator: O. Kharlampovich, R. Sklinos
description: Abstract We prove that a random group, in Gromov’s density model with d < 1 / 16 d<1/16 satisfies with overwhelming probability a universal-existential first-order sentence σ \sigma (in the language of groups) if and only if σ \sigma is true in a nonabelian free group.

title: FieldView: An interactive software tool for exploration of three-dimensional vector fields Journal: Software Impacts
creator: Piotr Nowakowski, Przemysław Rokita
description: Abstract Vector fields are one of the fundamental parts of mathematics which are key for modelling many physics phenomena such as electromagnetic fields or fluid and gas flows. Fields found in nature often exhibit complex structures which can be difficult to analyze in full detail without a graphical representation.

title: A mapping approach to surface hopping
creator: Jonathan R. Mannouch, Jeremy O. Richardson
description: Abstract We present a nonadiabatic classical-trajectory approach that offers the best of both worlds between fewest-switches surface hopping (FSSH) and quasiclassical mapping dynamics. This mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH) propagates the nuclei on the active adiabatic potential-energy surface, like in FSSH.

title: Pauli’s Electron in Ehrenfest and Bohm Theories, a Comparative Study
creator: Asher Yahalom
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Asher Yahalom. Electrons moving at slow speeds much lower that the speed of light are described by a wave function which is a solution of Pauli’s equation. This is a low velocity limit of the relativistic Dirac equation. Here we compare two approaches, one which is the more conservative Copenhagen’s interpretation denying a trajectory of the electron but allowing a trajectory to the electron expectation value through Ehrenfest theorem. The said expectation value is of course calculated using a solution of Pauli’s equation.

title: Analyticity of stationary spacetimes from maximal hypersurfaces Thanks: Vienna preprint UWThPh 2022-9 Thanks: Email marc@usal.es
creator: Piotr T. Chruściel
description: Abstract The standard method of proving analyticity of stationary vacuum metrics invokes the quotient-space version of Einstein equations. We verify that the same conclusion can be obtained using the KID equations on maximal surfaces. 1 Introduction A classical theorem of Morrey [ 15 ] asserts that solutions of a class of elliptic PDEs are real-analytic.

title: Compactness for a class of integral functionals with interacting local and non-local terms Thanks: Preprint SISSA 21/2022/MATE
creator: Andrea Braides, Gianni Dal Maso
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andrea Braides, Gianni Dal Maso. We prove a compactness result with respect to Γ \Gamma -convergence for a class of integral functionals which are expressed as a sum of a local and a non-local term. The main feature is that, under our hypotheses, the local part of the Γ \Gamma -limit depends on the interaction between the local and non-local terms of the converging subsequence. The result is applied to concentration and homogenization problems.

title: High-Resolution Transmission Spectroscopy of the Terrestrial Exoplanet GJ 486b Journal: AJ Facilities: 8.2 m Subaru telescope (IRD), 8.1 m Gemini-South telescope (IGRINS), 3.6 m Canada France Hawai’i Telescope (SPIRou) Astropy ( Astropy Collaboration et al. 2013 ; Astropy Collaboration et al. 2018 )
creator: Andrew Ridden-Harper, Stevanus K. Nugroho, Laura Flagg, Ray Jayawardhana, Jake D. Turner, Ernst de Mooij, Ryan MacDonald, Emily Deibert, Motohide Tamura, Takayuki Kotani, Teruyuki Hirano, Masayuki Kuzuhara, Masashi Omiya, Nobuhiko Kusakabe
description: Abstract Terrestrial exoplanets orbiting M-dwarf stars are promising targets for transmission spectroscopy with existing or near-future instrumentation. The atmospheric composition of such rocky planets remains an open question, especially given the high X-ray and ultraviolet flux from their host M dwarfs that can drive atmospheric escape. The 1.

title: Mesonic “screening masses" in high temperature QCD
creator: Edward Shuryak
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Edward Shuryak. Lattice studies of QCD at high temperature has investigated the so called “screening masses", corresponding to quark-antiquark states propagating in s ​ p ​ a ​ t ​ i ​ a ​ l spatial (rather than time) direction. Thirty years ago we pointed out that those should correspond to states of 2+1 dimensional quarkonia, and in this work we show that this correspondence provide quantitative description of the lattice data.

title: Analytical and numerical relaxation results for models in soil mechanics
creator: Florian Behr, Georg Dolzmann, Klaus Hackl, Ghina Jezdan
description: Abstract A variational model of pressure-dependent plasticity employing a time-incremental setting is introduced. A novel formulation of the dissipation potential allows one to construct the condensed energy in a variationally consistent manner. For a one-dimensional model problem, an explicit expression for the quasiconvex envelope can be found which turns out to be essentially independent of the original pressure-dependent yield surface.

title: A simple approach to hopping matrix elements between nearby molecules
creator: Shane Donaher, Puja Agarwala, Scott T. Milner
description: Abstract The hopping matrix element t t quantifies the quantum-mechanical coupling between frontier orbitals on a pair of nearby molecules. Convenient and generally applicable methods to determine t t from DFT calculations are lacking; t t can be obtained from coupling-induced energy splittings only if the interacting molecules are identical and symmetrically placed.

title: DYST ( Did You See That? ): An Amplified Covert Channel That Points To Previously Seen Data
creator: Steffen Wendzel, Tobias Schmidbauer, Sebastian Zillien, Jörg Keller
description: Abstract Covert channels are stealthy communication channels that enable manifold adversary and legitimate scenarios, ranging from malware communications to the exchange of confidential information by journalists and censorship circumvention. We introduce a new class of covert channels that we call history covert channels . We further present a new paradigm: covert channel amplification .

title: Phonon Self-Energy Corrections: To Screen, or Not to Screen
creator: Jan Berges, Nina Girotto, Tim Wehling, Nicola Marzari, Samuel Poncé
description: Abstract First-principles calculations of phonons are often based on the adiabatic approximation and on Brillouin-zone samplings that might not always be sufficient to capture the subtleties of Kohn anomalies. These shortcomings can be addressed through corrections to the phonon self-energy arising from the low-energy electrons.

title: Anisotropic electron transport in the nuclear pasta phase Anisotropic electron transport in the nuclear pasta phase – A 2022
creator: M. R. Pelicer, M. Antonelli, D. P. Menezes, F. Gulminelli
description: Abstract The presence of nuclear pasta is expected to modify the transport properties in the mantle of neutron stars. The non-spherical geometry of the pasta nuclear clusters leads to anisotropies in the collision frequencies, impacting the thermal and electrical conductivity. We derive analytical expressions for the anisotropic collision frequencies using the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation time approximation.

title: Differential Dynamic Microscopy can be applied to Differential Interference Contrast images despite shadowing effects
creator: Timothy Ostler, Wolfgang Langbein, Paola Borri, Emily Lewis, Yisu Wang, Karl Swann, Thomas E. Woolley, Katerina Kaouri
description: Abstract During In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF), combining time-lapse contrast microscopy with suitable image processing techniques could facilitate non-invasive classification of oocyte health, driving oocyte selection to maximise success rates. One image processing technique, Differential Dynamic Microscopy (DDM), has been used in a variety of microscopy settings including bright field, dark field and fluorescence.

title: Stability Analysis and Performance Evaluation of Mixed-Precision Runge-Kutta Methods Thanks: Submitted to the editors on December 15, 2022.
creator: Ben Burnett, Sigal Gottlieb*, Zachary J. Grant
description: Abstract Additive Runge-Kutta methods designed for preserving highly accurate solutions in mixed-precision computation were proposed and analyzed in [ 4 ] . These specially designed methods use reduced precision for the implicit computations and full precision for the explicit computations.

title: The Quantum Path Kernel: a Generalized Quantum Neural Tangent Kernel for Deep Quantum Machine Learning
creator: Massimiliano Incudini, Michele Grossi, Antonio Mandarino, Sofia Vallecorsa, Alessandra Di Pierro, David Windridge
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Massimiliano Incudini, Michele Grossi, Antonio Mandarino, Sofia Vallecorsa, Alessandra Di Pierro, David Windridge. Building a quantum analog of classical deep neural networks represents a fundamental challenge in quantum computing. A key issue is how to address the inherent non-linearity of classical deep learning, a problem in the quantum domain due to the fact that the composition of an arbitrary number of quantum gates, consisting of a series of sequential unitary transformations, is intrinsically linear.

title: Don’t Generate, Discriminate : A Proposal for Grounding Language Models to Real-World Environments
creator: Yu Gu, Xiang Deng, Yu Su
description: Abstract A key missing capacity of current language models (LMs) is grounding to real-world environments. Most existing work for grounded language understanding uses LMs to directly generate plans that can be executed in the environment to achieve the desired effects. It thereby casts the burden of ensuring grammaticality, faithfulness, and controllability all on the LMs.

title: p -forms from syzygies
creator: Alan Muniz
description: Abstract . These notes aim to develop a tool for constructing polynomial differential p p -forms vanishing on prescribed loci through syzygies of homogeneous ideals. Examples are provided through implementing this method in Macaulay2, particularly examples of instanton bundles of charges 4 4 and 5 5 on ℙ 3 {\mathbb{P}^{3}} that arise in this construction.

title: Multi-Frequency Channel Modeling for Millimeter Wave and THz Wireless Communication via Generative Adversarial Networks The authors were supported by NSF grants 1952180, 1925079, 1564142, 1547332, the SRC, OPPO, and the industrial affiliates of NYU WIRELESS. The work was also supported by Remcom tha
creator: Yaqi Hu, Mingsheng Yin, William Xia, Sundeep Rangan, Marco Mezzavilla
description: Abstract Modern cellular systems rely increasingly on simultaneous communication in multiple discontinuous bands for macro-diversity and increased bandwidth. Multi-frequency communication is particularly crucial in the millimeter wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) frequencies, as these bands are often coupled with lower frequencies for robustness.

title: Laser Cooling of Trapped Ions in Strongly Inhomogeneous Magnetic Fields
creator: Richard Karl, Yanning Yin and Stefan Willitsch
description: Abstract Hybrid traps for the simultaneous confinement of neutrals and ions have recently emerged as versatile tools for studying interactions between these species at very low temperatures. Such traps rely on the combination of different types of external fields for the confinement of either species raising the question of interactions between the individual traps.

title: Experimental Demonstration of Partially Disaggregated Optical Network Control Using the Physical Layer Digital Twin Thanks: Giacomo Borraccini, Renato Ambrosone, Emanuele Virgillito, Andrea D’Amico, Rocco D’Ingillio and Vittorio Curri are with the Department of Electronics and Telecommunications (DE
creator: Giacomo Borraccini, Stefano Straullu, Alessio Giorgetti
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Giacomo Borraccini, Stefano Straullu, Alessio Giorgetti. Optical communications and networking are fast becoming the solution to support ever-increasing data traffic across all segments of the network, expanding from core/metro networks to 5G/6G front-hauling. Therefore, optical networks need to evolve towards an efficient exploitation of the infrastructure by overcoming the closed and aggregated paradigm, to enable apparatus sharing together with the slicing and separation of the optical data plane from the optical control.

title: Aut ​ ( F n ) \text{Aut}(F_{n}) actions on representation spaces
creator: Tsachik Gelander
description: Abstract . J. Wiegold conjectured that if n ≥ 3 n\geq 3 and G G is a finite simple group, then the action of Aut ​ ( F n ) \text{Aut}(F_{n}) on Epi ​ ( F n , G ) \text{Epi}(F_{n},G) is transitive.

title: Zeros of a growing number of derivatives of random polynomials with independent roots
creator: Marcus Michelen, Xuan-Truong Vu
description: Abstract . Let X 1 , X 2 , … X_{1},X_{2},\ldots be independent and identically distributed random variables in ℂ {\mathbb{C}} chosen from a probability measure μ \mu and define the random polynomial P n ​ ( z ) = ( z − X 1 ) ​ … ​ ( z − X n ) . \displaystyle P_{n}(z)=(z-X_{1})\ldots(z-X_{n})\,.

title: Hint for a TeV neutrino emission from the Galactic Ridge with ANTARES Journal: Physics Letters B
creator: A. Albert, S. Alves, M. André, M. Ardid, S. Ardid, J.-J. Aubert, J. Aublin, B. Baret, S. Basa, Y. Becherini, B. Belhorma, M. Bendahman, F. Benfenati, V. Bertin, S. Biagi, M. Bissinger, J.
