description: Abstract We identify Greenlees’ C n C_{n} -equivariant connective K theory spectrum k ​ U C n kU_{C_{n}} as an R ​ O ​ ( C n ) RO(C_{n}) -graded localization of the actual connective cover of K ​ U C n KU_{C_{n}} .

title: Active queue management: First steps toward a new control-theoretic viewpoint
creator: Cédric JOIN a , e {a,e}, Hugues MOUNIER b {b}, Emmanuel DELALEAU c {c}, Michel FLIESS d , e {d,e}
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Cédric JOIN a , e {a,e}, Hugues MOUNIER b {b}, Emmanuel DELALEAU c {c}, Michel FLIESS d , e {d,e}. Active Queue Management (AQM) for mitigating Internet congestion has been addressed via various feedback control syntheses, among which P, PI, and PID regulators are quite popular and often associated to a Smith predictor.

title: Central Weyl involutions on Fano–Mukai fourfolds of genus 10 10
creator: Mikhail Zaidenberg
description: Abstract . It is known that every Fano–Mukai fourfold X X of genus 10 is acted upon by an involution τ \tau which comes from the center of the Weyl group of the simple algebraic group of type G 2 {\rm G}_{2} , see [ PZ18 , PZ22 ] .

title: Reflectance and fluorescence characteristics of PTFE coated with TPB at visible, UV, and VUV as a function of thickness
creator: J.T. White
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by J.T. White. Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is an excellent diffuse reflector widely used in light collection systems for particle physics experiments. In noble element systems, it is often coated with tetraphenyl butadiene (TPB) to allow detection of vacuum ultraviolet scintillation light. In this work this dependence is investigated for PTFE coated with TPB in air for light of wavelengths of 200 nm, 260 nm, and 450 nm.

title: Local Structure Matters Most in Most Languages
creator: Louis Clouâtre Prasanna Parthasarathi Amal Zouaq, Sarath Chandar
description: Abstract Many recent perturbation studies have found unintuitive results on what does and does not matter when performing Natural Language Understanding (NLU) tasks in English. Coding properties, such as the order of words, can often be removed through shuffling without impacting downstream performances. Such insight may be used to direct future research into English NLP models.

title: Detecting Languages Unintelligible to Multilingual Models through Local Structure Probes
creator: Louis Clouâtre Prasanna Parthasarathi Amal Zouaq, Sarath Chandar
description: Abstract Providing better language tools for low-resource and endangered languages is imperative for equitable growth. Recent progress with massively multilingual pretrained models has proven surprisingly effective at performing zero-shot transfer to a wide variety of languages. However, this transfer is not universal, with many languages not currently understood by multilingual approaches.

title: Fast and Scalable Channels in Kotlin Coroutines
creator: Nikita Koval, Dan Alistarh, Roman Elizarov
description: Abstract Asynchronous programming has gained significant popularity over the last decade: support for this programming pattern is available in many popular languages via libraries and native language implementations, typically in the form of coroutines or the async/await construct. Instead of programming via shared memory, this concept assumes implicit synchronization through message passing.

title: Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Readouts
creator: David Buterez 1 &Jon Paul Janet 2 &Steven J. Kiddle 3 &Dino Oglic 3 &Pietro Liò 1 & 1 Department of Computer Science and Technology, University of Cambridge, UK 2 CVRM, BioPharmaceuticals R&D, AstraZeneca, Sweden 3 DS&AI, BioPharmaceuticals R&D, AstraZeneca, UK
description: Abstract An effective aggregation of node features into a graph-level representation via readout functions is an essential step in numerous learning tasks involving graph neural networks. Typically, readouts are simple and non-adaptive functions designed such that the resulting hypothesis space is permutation invariant.

title: Internal DLA on mated-CRT maps
creator: Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Ewain Gwynne
description: Abstract . We prove a shape theorem for internal diffusion limited aggregation on mated-CRT maps, a family of random planar maps which approximate Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) surfaces. The limit is an LQG harmonic ball, which we constructed in a companion paper. We also prove an analogous result for the divisible sandpile. 1. Introduction Figure 1.

title: Ordered ground state configurations of the asymmetric Wigner bilayer system – revisited: an unsupervised clustering algorithm analysis
creator: Benedikt Hartl 1, Marek Mihalkovič 2, Ladislav Šamaj 2, Martial Mazars 3, Emmanuel Trizac 3, Gerhard Kahl 1
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Benedikt Hartl 1, Marek Mihalkovič 2, Ladislav Šamaj 2, Martial Mazars 3, Emmanuel Trizac 3, Gerhard Kahl 1. We have re-analysed the rich plethora of ground state configurations of the asymmetric Wigner bilayer system that we had recently published in a related diagram of states [M. 117 , 118002 (2016)], comprising roughly 60 000 state points in the phase space spanned by the distance between the plates and the charge asymmetry parameter of the system.

title: Magnetization reversal through an antiferromagnetic state
creator: S. Ghara, E. Barts, K. Vasin, D. Kamenskyi, L. Prodan, V. Tsurkan, I. Kézsmárki, M. Mostovoy, J. Deisenhofer
description: Abstract Magnetization reversal in ferro- and ferrimagnets is a well-known archetype of non-equilibrium processes, where the volume fractions of the oppositely magnetized domains vary and perfectly compensate each other at the coercive magnetic field. Here, we report on a fundamentally new pathway for magnetization reversal that is mediated by an antiferromagnetic state.

title: Are ultrafast inflows in AGN truly rare - or just much harder to see? Are ultrafast inflows in AGN truly rare - or just much harder to see? – References 2005 Are ultrafast inflows in AGN truly rare - or just much harder to see? – References
creator: Ken Pounds, Physics, Astronomy, University of Leicester, Leicester, LE1 7RH, UK
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ken Pounds, Physics, Astronomy, University of Leicester, Leicester, LE1 7RH, UK. Short-term variability and multiple velocity components in the powerful highly ionized wind of the archetypal UFO PG1211+143 are indicative of inner disc instabilities or short-lived accretion events.

title: Improving Performance of Automatic Keyword Extraction (AKE) Methods Using PoS-Tagging and Enhanced Semantic-Awareness
creator: Enes Altuncu, Jason R.C. Nurse, Yang Xu, Jie Guo, Shujun Li
description: Abstract Automatic keyword extraction (AKE) has gained more importance with the increasing amount of digital textual data that modern computing systems process. It has various applications in information retrieval (IR) and natural language processing (NLP), including text summarisation, topic analysis and document indexing.

title: Combining Contrastive Learning and Knowledge Graph Embeddings to develop medical word embeddings for the Italian language
creator: Denys Amore Bondarenko, Roger Ferrod, Luigi Di Caro
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Denys Amore Bondarenko, Roger Ferrod, Luigi Di Caro. Word embeddings play a significant role in today’s Natural Language Processing tasks and applications. While pre-trained models may be directly employed and integrated into existing pipelines, they are often fine-tuned to better fit with specific languages or domains. In this paper, we attempt to improve available embeddings in the uncovered niche of the Italian medical domain through the combination of Contrastive Learning (CL) and Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE).

title: On a conjecture of Franušić and Jadrijević: Counter-examples
creator: Kalyan Chakraborty, Shubham Gupta and Azizul Hoque

title: A Comparative Study of Data Augmentation Techniques for Deep Learning Based Emotion Recognition
creator: Ravi Shankar, Abdouh Harouna Kenfack, Arjun Somayazulu, Archana Venkataraman
description: Abstract Automated emotion recognition in speech is a long-standing problem. While early work on emotion recognition relied on hand-crafted features and simple classifiers, the field has now embraced end-to-end feature learning and classification using deep neural networks. In parallel to these models, researchers have proposed several data augmentation techniques to increase the size and variability of existing labeled datasets.

title: MACSum : Controllable Summarization with Mixed Attributes
creator: Yusen Zhang, Yang Liu, Ziyi Yang, Yuwei Fang Yulong Chen Dragomir Radev, Chenguang Zhu Michael Zeng Rui Zhang
description: Abstract Controllable summarization allows users to generate customized summaries with specified attributes. However, due to the lack of designated annotations of controlled summaries, existing works have to craft pseudo datasets by adapting generic summarization benchmarks. Furthermore, most research focuses on controlling single attributes individually (e.g.

title: Precision Measurements of Atom-Dimer Interactions in a Uniform Planar Bose Gas
creator: C. Maury, B. Bakkali-Hassani, G. Chauveau, F. Rabec, S. Nascimbene, J. Dalibard, J. Beugnon
description: Abstract Cold quantum gases, when acted upon by electromagnetic fields, can give rise to samples where isolated atoms coexist with dimers or trimers, which raises the question of the interactions between these various constituents. Here we perform microwave photoassociation in a degenerate gas of 87 Rb atoms to create weakly-bound dimers in their electronic ground state.

title: Randomization of Short-Rate Models, Analytic Pricing and Flexibility in Controlling Implied Volatilities
creator: LECH A. GRZELAK
description: Abstract We focus on extending existing short-rate models, enabling control of the generated implied volatility while preserving analyticity. We achieve this goal by applying the Randomized Affine Diffusion (RAnD) method [ 10 ] to the class of short-rate processes under the Heath-Jarrow-Morton framework.

title: Accountable and Explainable Methods for Complex Reasoning over Text
creator: Pepa Kostadinova Atanasova Supervised by Isabelle Augenstein, Jakob Grue Simonsen and Christina Lioma
description: Abstract \subject This thesis has been submitted to the PhD School of The Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen Abstract A major concern of Machine Learning (ML) models is their opacity. They are deployed in an increasing number of applications where they often operate as black boxes that do not provide explanations for their predictions.

title: Extended explanation of Orevkov’s paper on proper holomorphic embeddings of complements of Cantor sets in ℂ 2 \mathbb{C}^{2} and a discussion of their measure.
creator: Giovanni D. Di Salvo
description: Abstract . We clarify the details of a cryptical paper by Orevkov in which a construction of a proper holomorphic embedding γ : ℙ 1 ∖ C ↪ ℂ 2 \gamma\colon\mathbb{P}^{1}\setminus C\hookrightarrow\mathbb{C}^{2} is presented; in particular, it is proved that such a construction can be done to get the Cantor set C C to have zero Hausdorff dimension.

title: A flux-differencing formulation with Gauss nodes Journal: Journal of Computational Physics

description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andrés Mateo-Gabín, Andrés M. Rueda-Ramírez, Eusebio Valero, Gonzalo Rubio. 1 Introduction Among the different spatial discretization frameworks, the Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Element Method (DGSEM) [ 1 , 2 ] approximates a function as a set of discontinuous, high-order polynomials defined in a tessellation of the spatial domain. The DGSEM is a collocation method that represents the solution as a combination of Lagrange polynomials that shares the nodes with a certain quadrature rule, usually Gauss or Gauss-Lobatto.

title: Galois Hull Dimensions of Gabidulin Codes Thanks: H. Islam and A-L. Horlemann are with School of Computer Science, University of St. Gallen, Switzerland, (e-mail: habibul.islam@unisg.ch, anna-lena.horlemann@unisg.ch).
creator: Habibul Islam, Anna-Lena Horlemann
description: Abstract For a prime power q q , an integer m m and 0 ≤ e ≤ m − 1 0\leq e\leq m-1 we study the e e -Galois hull dimension of Gabidulin codes G k ​ ( 𝜶 ) G_{k}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) of length m m and dimension k k over 𝔽 q m \mathbb{F}_{q^{m}} .

title: Black-Box Model Confidence Sets Using Cross-Validation with High-Dimensional Gaussian Comparison
creator: Nicholas Kissel, Jing Lei
description: Abstract We derive high-dimensional Gaussian comparison results for the standard V V -fold cross-validated risk estimates. Our results combine a recent stability-based argument for the low-dimensional central limit theorem of cross-validation with the high-dimensional Gaussian comparison framework for sums of independent random variables.

title: Land Use Trade-offs in Decarbonization of Electricity Generation in the American West
creator: Neha Patankar, Xiili Sarkela-Basset, Greg Schivley, Emily Leslie, Jesse Jenkins
description: Abstract Land-use conflicts may constrain the unprecedented rates of renewable energy deployment required to meet the decarbonization goals of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA). This paper employs geospatially resolved data and a detailed electricity system capacity expansion model to generate 160 affordable, zero-carbon electricity supply portfolios for the American west and evaluates the land use impacts of each portfolio.

title: On the effect of localized and delocalized quasiparticles on a nonlinear conductivity of superconductors
creator: A. Gurevich
description: Abstract Recently Deyo et al. [Phys. Rev. B 106 , 104502 (2022)] suggested that the surface resistance R s ​ ( H 0 ) R_{s}(H_{0}) of a superconductor under strong electromagnetic field can be affected by field-induced quasiparticle bound states at the surface.

title: A flexible class of exact Hubbard-Stratonovich transformations
creator: Seher Karakuzu, Benjamin Cohen-Stead, Cristian D. Batista, Steven Johnston, Kipton Barros
description: Abstract We consider a class of Hubbard-Stratonovich transformations suitable for treating Hubbard interactions in the context of quantum Monte Carlo simulations. A tunable parameter p p allows us to continuously vary from a discrete Ising auxiliary field ( p = ∞ p=\infty ) to a compact auxiliary field that couples to electrons sinusoidally ( p = 0 p=0 ).

title: A Diffeomorphic Flow-based Variational Framework for Multi-speaker Emotion Conversion
creator: Ravi Shankar, Hsi-Wei Hsieh, Nicolas Charon, and Archana Venkataraman
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ravi Shankar, Hsi-Wei Hsieh, Nicolas Charon, and Archana Venkataraman. This paper introduces a new framework for non-parallel emotion conversion in speech. Our framework is based on two key contributions. First, we propose a stochastic version of the popular Cycle-GAN model. Our modified loss function introduces a Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence term that aligns the source and target data distributions learned by the generators, thus overcoming the limitations of sample-wise generation.

title: Large area LaBr3:Ce crystals read by SiPM arrays with improved timing and temperature gain drift control Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
creator: M. Bonesini, R. Benocci, R. Bertoni, A. Menegolli, M. Prata, M. Rossella, R. Rossini
description: Abstract Compact X-rays detectors made of 1/2" or 1" :LaBr 3 :Ce crystals of cubic shape with SiPM array readout have been developed for the FAMU experiment at RIKEN-RAL. The aim is a precise measurement of the proton Zemach radius with incoming muons. Additional applications may be found in medical physics, such as PET, homeland security and gamma-ray astronomy.

title: Warm Inflation in f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity
creator: Biswajit Deb, Sabina Yeasmin, Atri DeshamukhyaDepartment of Physics, Assam University, Silchar, India
description: Abstract In this work, we explored warm inflation in the background of f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity in the strong dissipation regime. Considering scalar field for FLRW universe, we derived modified field equations. We then deduced slow-roll parameters under slow-roll approximations followed by power spectrum for scalar and tensor perturbations and their corresponding spectral indices.

title: Automated Learning: An Implementation of The A* Search Algorithm over The Random Base Functions
creator: Nima Tatari
description: Abstract 1 Introduction The presented idea resembles the asymptotic series representation of a target function as opposed to the convergent series representation, such as the Taylor series. In the asymptotic expansion, the first few terms of the series represent the target function behavior with the desired accuracy in the asymptotic regime [ 1 ] .

title: Axion-pion thermalization rate in unitarized NLO chiral perturbation theory
creator: Luca Di Luzio, Jorge Martin Camalich, Guido Martinelli, José Antonio Oller, Gioacchino Piazza
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luca Di Luzio, Jorge Martin Camalich, Guido Martinelli, José Antonio Oller, Gioacchino Piazza. We compute the axion-pion scattering a ​ π → π ​ π a\pi\to\pi\pi , relevant for the axion thermalization rate in the early universe, within unitarized NLO chiral perturbation theory.

title: A Nearly Time-Optimal Distributed Approximation of Minimum Cost k k -Edge-Connected Spanning Subgraph
creator: Michal Dory, Mohsen Ghaffari
description: Abstract The minimum-cost k k -edge-connected spanning subgraph ( k k -ECSS) problem is a generalization and strengthening of the well-studied minimum-cost spanning tree (MST) problem. While the round complexity of distributedly computing the latter has been well-understood, the former remains mostly open, especially as soon as k ≥ 3 k\geq 3 .

title: Clinical Contrastive Learning for Biomarker Detection
creator: Kiran Kokilepersaud, Mohit Prabhushankar, Ghassan AlRegib
description: Abstract This paper presents a novel positive and negative set selection strategy for contrastive learning of medical images based on labels that can be extracted from clinical data . In the medical field, there exists a variety of labels for data that serve different purposes at different stages of a diagnostic and treatment process.

title: Mirror Surface Nanostructuring via Laser Direct Writing - Characterization and Physical Origins
creator: Mario Vretenar, Jan Klaers
description: Abstract The addition of an optically absorptive layer to otherwise standard dielectric mirrors enables a set of laser direct writing nanostructuring methods that can add functionality to such mirrors while retaining their high reflectivity. These mirrors are particularly suited for use in optical microcavities, where arbitrary potential landscapes for photons may be constructed.

title: Free-fermions and canonical Grothendieck polynomials Thanks: S.I. was partially supported by Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C) 19K03605. K.M. was partially supported by Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C) 21K03176, 20K03793. T.S. was partially supported by Grant-in-Aid for JSPS Fellows 2
creator: Shinsuke Iwao, Kohei Motegi, Travis Scrimshaw
description: Abstract . We give a presentation of refined (dual) canonical Grothendieck polynomials and their skew versions using free-fermions. Using this, we derive a number of identities, including the skew Cauchy identities, branching rules, expansion formulas, and integral formulas. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 05E05, 82B23, 14M15, 05A19 1.

title: Generalized Lagrangian Heterogenous Multiscale Modeling of Complex Fluids
creator: Nicolas Moreno ∗ *, Marco Ellero † \dagger 1.Basque Center for Applied Mathematics (BCAM), Alameda de Mazarredo 14, Bilbao 48400, Spain 2. IKERBASQUE, Basque Foundation for Science, Calle de Maria Dias de Haro 3, 48013, Bilbao, Spain 3. Zienkiewicz Center for Computational Engineering (ZCCE), Swanse
description: Abstract We introduce a full-Lagrangian heterogeneous multiscale method (LHMM) to model complex fluids with microscopic features that can extend over large spatio/temporal scales, such as polymeric solutions and multiphasic systems. The proposed approach discretizes the fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations in a particle-based setting using Smoothed Dissipative Particle Dynamics (SDPD).

title: Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen experiment with two Bose-Einstein condensates
creator: Paolo Colciaghi, Yifan Li, Philipp Treutlein, Tilman Zibold
description: Abstract In 1935, Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen (EPR) conceived a Gedankenexperiment which became a cornerstone of quantum technology and still challenges our understanding of reality and locality today. While the experiment has been realized with small quantum systems, a demonstration of the EPR paradox with spatially separated, massive many-particle systems has so far remained elusive.

title: Geometric Properties of Generalized Hypergeometric Functions
creator: K. Chandrasekran, D.J. Prabhakaran
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by K. Chandrasekran, D.J. Prabhakaran. In this article, Using Hadamard product for F 3 4 ( ; b 1 , b 2 , b 3 a 1 , a 2 , a 3 , a 4 z ) {}_{4}F_{3}\left({}^{a_{1},\,a_{2},\,a_{3},\,a_{4}}_{b_{1},\,b_{2},\,b_{3}};z\right) hypergeometric function with normalized analytic functions in the open unit disc, an operator ℐ b 1 , b 2 , b 3 a 1 , a 2 , a 3 , a 4 ​ ( f ) ​ ( z ) \mathcal{I}^{a_{1},a_{2},a_{3},a_{4}}_{b_{1},b_{2},b_{3}}(f)(z) is introduced.

title: Accidental Learners: Spoken Language Identification in Multilingual Self-Supervised Models
creator: Travis M. Bartley, Fei Jia, Krishna C. Puvvada, Samuel Kriman, Boris Ginsburg
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Travis M. Bartley, Fei Jia, Krishna C. Puvvada, Samuel Kriman, Boris Ginsburg. In this paper, we extend previous self-supervised approaches for language identification by experimenting with Conformer based architecture in a multilingual pre-training paradigm. We find that pre-trained speech models optimally encode language discriminatory information in lower layers. Further, we demonstrate that the embeddings obtained from these layers are significantly robust to classify unseen languages and different acoustic environments without additional training.

title: From Minkowski to de Sitter Vacua with Various Geometries
creator: Constantinos Pallis Laboratory of Physics, Faculty of Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, GR-541 24 Thessaloniki, GREECE e-mail address: kpallis@gen.auth.gr
description: Abstract Abstract: New no-scale supergravity models with F-term SUSY breaking are introduced, adopting Kähler potentials parameterizing flat or curved (compact or non-compact) Kähler manifolds. We systematically derive the form of the superpotentials leading to Minkowski vacua. Combining two types of these superpotentials we can also determine de Sitter or anti-de Sitter vacua.

title: Scalar curvatures of invariant almost Hermitian structures on flag manifolds with two and three isotropic summands
creator: Lino Grama, Ailton R. Oliveira
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lino Grama, Ailton R. Oliveira. In this paper we study invariant almost Hermitian geometry on generalized flag manifolds which the isotropy representation decompose into two or three irreducible components. We will provide a classification of such flag manifolds admitting Kähler like scalar curvature metric , that is, almost Hermitian structures ( g , J ) (g,J) satisfying s = 2 ​ s C s=2s_{C} where s s is Riemannian scalar curvature and s C s_{C} is the Chern scalar curvature.

title: Assessment of kinetic theories for moderately dense granular binary mixtures: Shear viscosity coefficient
creator: Moisés García Chamorro, Vicente Garzó
description: Abstract Two different kinetic theories [J. Solsvik and E. Manger (SM), Phys. Fluids 33 , 043321 (2021) and V. Garzó, J. W. Dufty, and C. M. Hrenya (GDH), Phys. Rev. E 76 , 031303 (2007)] are considered to determine the shear viscosity η \eta for a moderately dense granular binary mixture of smooth hard spheres.

title: Large Language Models with Controllable Working Memory
creator: Daliang Li, Ankit Singh Rawat, Manzil Zaheer,Xin Wang, Michal Lukasik, Andreas Veit, Felix Yu, Sanjiv Kumar
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have led to a series of breakthroughs in natural language processing (NLP), owing to their excellent understanding and generation abilities. Remarkably, what further sets these models apart is the massive amounts of world knowledge they internalize during pretraining.

title: Reiner Pope
description: Abstract We study the problem of efficient generative inference for Transformer models, in one of its most challenging settings: large deep models, with tight latency targets and long sequence lengths. Better understanding of the engineering tradeoffs for inference for large Transformer-based models is important as use cases of these models are growing rapidly throughout application areas.

title: Small scale formation for the 2D Boussinesq equation Thanks: Department of Mathematics, Duke University, 120 Science Dr., Durham NC 27708, USA; email: kiselev@math.duke.edu Thanks: Department of Mathematics and Computer Science, University of Basel, Spiegelgasse 1, 4051 Basel, Switzerland. email: ja
creator: Alexander Kiselev, Jaemin Park, Yao Yao
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexander Kiselev, Jaemin Park, Yao Yao. We study the 2D incompressible Boussinesq equation without thermal diffusion, and aim to construct rigorous examples of small scale formations as time goes to infinity. In the viscous case, we construct examples of global smooth solutions satisfying sup τ ∈ [ 0 , t ] ‖ ∇ ρ ​ ( τ ) ‖ L 2 ≳ t α \sup_{\tau\in[0,t]}\|\nabla\rho(\tau)\|_{L^{2}}\gtrsim t^{\alpha} for some α > 0 \alpha>0 .

title: A Note on Task-Aware Loss via Reweighing Prediction Loss by Decision-Regret
creator: Connor LawlessCornell University, Angela ZhouUSC Marshall School of Business
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Connor LawlessCornell University, Angela ZhouUSC Marshall School of Business. In this short technical note we propose a baseline for decision-aware learning for contextual linear optimization, which solves stochastic linear optimization when cost coefficients can be predicted based on context information. We propose a decision-aware version of predict-then-optimize. We reweigh the prediction error by the decision regret incurred by an (unweighted) pilot estimator of costs to obtain a decision-aware predictor , then optimize with cost predictions from the decision-aware predictor.

title: Mapping Out the HPC Dependency Chaos
creator: Farid Zakaria 1 , Thomas R. W. Scogland 2 , Todd Gamblin 2 , Carlos Maltzahn 1
description: Abstract High Performance Computing (HPC) software stacks have become complex, with the dependencies of some applications numbering in the hundreds. Packaging, distributing, and administering software stacks of that scale is a complex undertaking anywhere. HPC systems deal with esoteric compilers, hardware, and a panoply of uncommon combinations.

title: BLOOM: A 176B-Parameter Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
creator: BigScience Workshop, Major Contributors, Dataset, Tokenization, Prompt Engineering, Architecture, Objective, Engineering, Evaluation, Interpretability, Broader Impacts, Applications, Organization
description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have been shown to be able to perform new tasks based on a few demonstrations or natural language instructions. While these capabilities have led to widespread adoption, most LLMs are developed by resource-rich organizations and are frequently kept from the public.

title: Deep Learning based Computer Vision Methods for Complex Traffic Environments Perception: A Review Thanks: Talha Azfar is with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Texas at El Paso, El Paso, TX, 79968 USA, e-mail: tazfar@miners.utep.edu. Jinlong Li and Hongkai Yu are w
creator: Talha Azfar, Jinlong Li, Hongkai Yu, Ruey Long Cheu
description: Abstract Computer vision applications in intelligent transportation systems (ITS) and autonomous driving (AD) have gravitated towards deep neural network architectures in recent years. While performance seems to be improving on benchmark datasets, many real-world challenges are yet to be adequately considered in research.

title: TECHNICAL REPORT: Sparse Bayesian Lasso via a Variable-Coefficient ℓ 1 \ell_{1} Penalty
creator: Nathan Wycoff, Ali Arab, Katharine M. Donato, Lisa O. Singh
description: Abstract Modern statistical learning algorithms are capable of amazing flexibility, but struggle with interpretability. One possible solution is sparsity : making inference such that many of the parameters are estimated as being identically 0 0 , which may be imposed through the use of nonsmooth penalties such as the ℓ 1 \ell_{1} penalty.

title: ChromoSkein: Untangling Three-Dimensional Chromatin Fiber With a Web-Based Visualization Framework Thanks: M. Talčík, F. Opálený, K. Furmanová, B. Kozlíková, D. Kouřil are with Masaryk University, Brno, Czechia. J. Byška is with Masaryk University, Brno, Czechia and University of Bergen, Bergen, Nor
creator: Matúš Talčík, Filip Opálený, Tereza Clarence, Katarína Furmanová, Jan Byška
description: Abstract We present ChromoSkein, a web-based tool for visualizing three-dimensional chromatin models. The spatial organization of chromatin is essential to its function. Experimental methods, namely Hi-C, reveal the spatial conformation but output a 2D matrix representation. Biologists leverage simulation to bring this information back to 3D, assembling a 3D chromatin shape prediction using the 2D matrices as constraints.

title: Regulation of Star Formation by a Hot Circumgalactic Medium
creator: Christopher Carr, Greg L. Bryan, Drummond B. Fielding, Viraj Pandya, Rachel S. Somerville
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Christopher Carr, Greg L. Bryan, Drummond B. Fielding, Viraj Pandya, Rachel S. Somerville. Galactic outflows driven by supernovae (SNe) are thought to be a powerful regulator of a galaxy’s star-forming efficiency. Mass, energy, and metal outflows ( η M \eta_{M} , η E \eta_{E} , and η Z \eta_{Z} , here normalized by the star formation rate, the SNe energy and metal production rates, respectively) shape galaxy properties by both ejecting gas and metals out of the galaxy and by heating the circumgalactic medium

title: Safe Latent Diffusion: Mitigating Inappropriate Degeneration in Diffusion Models
creator: Patrick Schramowski, Manuel Brack, Björn Deiseroth, Kristian Kersting
description: Abstract Text-conditioned image generation models have recently achieved astonishing results in image quality and text alignment and are consequently employed in a fast-growing number of applications. Since they are highly data-driven, relying on billion-sized datasets randomly scraped from the internet, they also suffer, as we demonstrate, from degenerated and biased human behavior. In turn, they may even reinforce such biases.

title: ViTALiTy: Unifying Low-rank and Sparse Approximation for Vi sion T ransformer A cceleration with a Li near T a y lor Attention
creator: Jyotikrishna Dass* 2 , Shang Wu* 2 , Huihong Shi* 3 , Chaojian Li 3 , Zhifan Ye 2 , Zhongfeng Wang 4 and Yingyan Lin 3
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jyotikrishna Dass* 2 , Shang Wu* 2 , Huihong Shi* 3 , Chaojian Li 3 , Zhifan Ye 2 , Zhongfeng Wang 4 and Yingyan Lin 3. Vision Transformer (ViT) has emerged as a competitive alternative to convolutional neural networks for various computer vision applications. Specifically, ViTs’ multi-head attention layers make it possible to embed information globally across the overall image.

title: SN 2022ann: A type Icn supernova from a dwarf galaxy that reveals helium in its circumstellar environment 2022 SN 2022ann: A type Icn supernova from a dwarf galaxy that reveals helium in its circumstellar environment – B
creator: K. W. Davis, K. Taggart, S. Tinyanont, R. J. Foley, V. A. Villar, L. Izzo, C. R. Angus, M. J. Bustamante-Rosell, D. A. Coulter, N. Earl, D. Farias, J. Hjorth, M. E. Huber, D. O. Jones, P. L. Kelly, C. D. Kilpatrick, D. Langeroodi, H.-Y. Miao, C. M. Pellegrino, E. Ramirez-Ruiz, C. L. Ransome, S. Rest
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by K. W. Davis, K. Taggart, S. Tinyanont, R. J. Foley, V. A. Villar, L. Izzo, C. R. Angus, M. J. Bustamante-Rosell, D. A. Coulter, N. Earl, D. Farias, J. Hjorth, M. E. Huber, D. O. Jones, P. L. Kelly, C. D. Kilpatrick, D. Langeroodi, H.-Y. Miao, C. M. Pellegrino, E. Ramirez-Ruiz, C. L. Ransome, S. Rest. We present optical and near-infrared (NIR) observations of the Type Icn supernova (SN Icn) 2022ann, the fifth member of its newly identified class of SNe.

title: On Berman functions
creator: Krzysztof Dȩbicki, Enkelejd Hashorva, Zbigniew Michna
description: Abstract Abstract: Let Z(t)=\exp\left(\sqrt{2}B_{H}(t)-\left\lvert t\right\rvert^{2H}\right),t\in\mathbb{R} with B_{H}(t),t\in\mathbb{R} a standard fractional Brownian motion (fBm) with Hurst parameter H\in(0,1] and define for x non-negative the Berman function \displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{Z}(x)=\mathbb{E}\left\{\frac{\mathbb{I}{\left\{\epsilon_{0}(RZ)>x\right\}}}{\epsilon_{0}(RZ)}\right\}\in(0,\infty), where the random variable R independent of Z has survival function 1/x,x\geq 1 and \epsilon_{0}(RZ)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\mathbb{I}{\left\{RZ(t)>1\right\}}dt.

title: Projected spin texture as a bulk indicator of fragile topology
creator: Gunnar F. Lange, Adrien Bouhon, Robert-Jan Slager
description: Abstract We study the relationship between projected momentum-space spin textures and Wilson loop winding, proving a map between band topology of and spin topology in certain restricted symmetry settings, relevant to fragile topology. Our results suggest that the spin gap may act as a smoking gun bulk indicator for fragile topology within specific scenarios. Introduction.

title: Toward extracting 𝜸 \gamma from 𝑩 → 𝑫 ​ 𝑲 B\to DK without binning
creator: Jeffrey V. Backus, Marat Freytsis, Yuval Grossman, Stefan Schacht, Jure Zupan
description: Abstract B ± → D ​ K ± B^{\pm}\to DK^{\pm} transitions are known to provide theoretically clean information about the CKM angle γ \gamma , with the most precise available methods exploiting the cascade decay of the neutral D D into C ​ P CP self-conjugate states.

title: Toward Horizon-scale Accretion onto Supermassive Black Holes in Elliptical Galaxies Athena++ ( Stone et al. 2020 ) ,
creator: Minghao Guo (郭明浩), James M. Stone, Chang-Goo Kim, Eliot Quataert
description: Abstract We present high-resolution, three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of the fueling of supermassive black holes in elliptical galaxies from a turbulent medium on galactic scales, taking M87* as a typical case. The simulations use a new GPU-accelerated version of the Athena++ AMR code, and span more than 6 orders of magnitude in radius, reaching scales similar to the black hole horizon.

title: Comparing Accretion Disks and Dark Matter Spikes in Intermediate Mass Ratio Inspirals
creator: Niklas Becker, Laura Sagunski
description: Abstract Intermediate Mass Ratio Inspirals (IMRIs) will be observable with space-based gravitational wave detectors such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). To this end, the environmental effects in such systems have to be modeled and understood. These effects can include (baryonic) accretion disks and dark matter (DM) overdensities, so called spikes .

title: Attention to the strengths of physical interactions: Transformer and graph-based event classification for particle physics experiments
creator: Luc Builtjes, Sascha Caron, Polina Moskvitina, Clara Nellist, Roberto Ruiz de Austri, Rob Verheyen, Zhongyi Zhang
description: Abstract A major task in particle physics is the measurement of rare signal processes. These measurements are highly dependent on the classification accuracy of these events in relation to the huge background of other Standard Model processes. Reducing the background by a few tens of percent with the same signal efficiency can already increase the sensitivity considerably.

title: Engineering axion insulator and other topological phases in superlattices without inversion symmetry
creator: Rajibul Islam ID, Sougata Mardanya, Alexander Lau ID, Giuseppe Cuono ID, Tay-Rong Chang ID, Bahadur Singh ID, Carlo M. Canali ID, Tomasz Dietl ID, Carmine Autieri ID
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Rajibul Islam ID, Sougata Mardanya, Alexander Lau ID, Giuseppe Cuono ID, Tay-Rong Chang ID, Bahadur Singh ID, Carlo M. Canali ID, Tomasz Dietl ID, Carmine Autieri ID. We study theoretically the interplay between magnetism and topology in three-dimensional HgTe/MnTe superlattices stacked along the (001) axis. Our results show the evolution of the magnetic topological phases with respect to the magnetic configurations.

title: Efficient Zero-shot Event Extraction with Context-Definition Alignment
creator: Hongming Zhang, Wenlin Yao, Dong Yu
description: Abstract Event extraction (EE) is the task of identifying interested event mentions from text. Conventional efforts mainly focus on the supervised setting. However, these supervised models cannot generalize to event types out of the pre-defined ontology. To fill this gap, many efforts have been devoted to the zero-shot EE problem.

title: Neutral B B -anomalies from an on-shell scalar exchange
creator: J. Bonilla, A. de Giorgi, M. Ramos
description: Abstract The neutral B B -anomalies are analysed in terms of the tree-level exchange of a (pseudo)scalar gauge singlet a a . Solutions to both R K ( ∗ ) R_{K^{(*)}} central bin anomalies are found within 1 ​ σ 1\sigma for m a 2 ∈ [ 1.1 , 6 ] ​ GeV 2 {m_{a}^{2}\in[{1.

title: Volumetric rates of Luminous Red Novae and Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients with the Zwicky Transient Facility
creator: Viraj R. Karambelkar, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Nadejda Blagorodnova, Jesper Sollerman, Robert Aloisi, Shreya G. Anand, Igor Andreoni, Thomas G. Brink, Rachel Bruch, David Cook, Kaustav Kashyap Das, Kishalay De, Andrew Drake, Alexei V. Filippenko, Christoffer Fremling, George Helou, Anna Ho, Jacob Jencson,
description: Abstract Luminous red novae (LRNe) are transients characterized by low luminosities and expansion velocities, and are associated with mergers or common envelope ejections in stellar binaries. Intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs) are an observationally similar class with unknown origins, but generally believed to either be electron capture supernovae (ECSN) in super-AGB stars, or outbursts in dusty luminous blue variables (LBVs).

title: Uncertainties in the Transport Properties of Helium Gas at Cryogenic Temperatures Determined Using Molecular Dynamics Simulation
creator: Kaanapuli Ramkumar, Swati Swagatika Mishra, Sudeep Bhattacharjee
description: Abstract In this study, the transport properties, such as diffusivity, viscosity, and thermal conductivity, of 4 He at the gaseous phase are computed for state points in the temperature range of 10 K to 150 K and pressure range of 0.10 MPa (1 atm) to 0.21 MPa using classical and quantum frameworks.

title: Topological exodromy with coefficients
creator: Mauro PORTA, Jean-Baptiste Teyssier
description: Abstract . We improve the exodromy equivalence of MacPherson, Treumann and Lurie in several ways: first, we allow stratified spaces that have locally weakly contractible strata, rather than being locally of singular shape, we remove all noetherianity assumptions and we consider more general coefficients (e.g. compactly assembled or stable presentable ∞ \infty -categories).

title: Millicharged Relics Reveal Massless Dark Photons
creator: Asher Berlin, Jeff A. Dror, Xucheng Gan, Joshua T. Ruderman
description: Abstract The detection of massless kinetically-mixed dark photons is notoriously difficult, as the effect of this mixing can be removed by a field redefinition in vacuum. In this work, we study the prospect of detecting massless dark photons in the presence of a cosmic relic directly charged under this dark electromagnetism.

title: Uni-Parser: Unified Semantic Parser for Question Answering on Knowledge Base and Database
creator: Ye Liu, Semih Yavuz, Rui Meng, Dragomir Radev, Caiming Xiong, Yingbo Zhou
description: Abstract Parsing natural language questions into executable logical forms is a useful and interpretable way to perform question answering on structured data such as knowledge bases (KB) or databases (DB). However, existing approaches on semantic parsing cannot adapt to both modalities, as they suffer from the exponential growth of the logical form candidates and can hardly generalize to unseen data.

title: Fracton Matter
creator: Andrey Gromov, Leo Radzihovsky
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Andrey Gromov, Leo Radzihovsky. We review a burgeoning field of “fractons” - a class of models where quasi-particles are strictly immobile or display restricted mobility that can be understood through generalized multipolar symmetries and associated conservation laws. Focusing on just a corner of this fast-growing subject, we will demonstrate how one class of such theories - symmetric tensor and coupled-vector gauge theories surprisingly emerge from familiar elasticity of a two-dimensional quantum crystal.

title: The [ 1 , 0 ] [1,0] -twisted generalized Reed-Solomon code
creator: Canze Zhu 1, Qunying Liao 2
description: Abstract Abstract. In this paper, we not only give the parity check matrix of the [1,0] -twisted generalized Reed-Solomon (in short, TGRS) code, but also determine the weight distribution. Especially, we show that the [1,0] -TGRS code is not GRS or EGRS.

title: Precision Bounds on Continuous-Variable State Tomography using Classical Shadows
creator: Srilekha Gandhari, Victor V. Albert, Thomas Gerrits, Jacob M. Taylor, Michael J. Gullans
description: Abstract Shadow tomography is a framework for constructing succinct descriptions of quantum states using randomized measurement bases , called classical shadows, with powerful methods to bound the estimators used. We recast existing experimental protocols for continuous-variable quantum state tomography in the classical-shadow framework, obtaining rigorous bounds on the number of independent measurements needed for estimating density matrices from these protocols.

title: Superconductivity in monolayer and few-layer graphene: I. Review of possible pairing symmetries and basic electronic properties
creator: Emile Pangburn, Louis Haurie, Adeline Crépieux, Oladunjoye A. Awoga, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, Catherine Pépin, Cristina Bena
description: Abstract We review all symmetry-allowed spin-singlet and spin-triplet superconducting (SC) order parameters in graphene ( s s -wave, d d -wave, p p -wave, and f f -wave) generated by generic onsite, nearest-neighbor (NN), and next-to-nearest-neighbor (NNN) pairing interactions in a tight-binding model.

title: Are All Edges Necessary? A Unified Framework for Graph Purification
creator: Zishan Gu, Jintang Li, Liang Chen
description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) as deep learning models working on graph-structure data have achieved advanced performance in many works. However, it has been proved repeatedly that, not all edges in a graph are necessary for the training of machine learning models.

title: Integral Curvature Bounds and Betti Numbers
creator: Runze Yu
description: Abstract . We introduce an upper bound of the Betti numbers of a compact Riemannian manifold given integral bounds on the average of the lowest eigenvalues of the curvature operator. We then establish a new curvature condition for the Betti numbers to vanish using the Bochner technique. This generalizes results from Gallot and Petersen-Wink.

title: Modeling Motivational Interviewing Strategies On An Online Peer-to-Peer Counseling Platform Journal: PACMHCI Volume: 6 CSCW2 527 11 DOI: 10.1145/3555640 CCS: Human-centered computing HCI theory, concepts and models CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in collaborative and social computing
creator: Raj Sanjay Shah, Faye Holt, Shirley Anugrah Hayati, Aastha Agarwal, Yi-Chia Wang, Robert E. Kraut, Diyi Yang
description: Abstract . Millions of people participate in online peer-to-peer support sessions, yet there has been little prior research on systematic psychology-based evaluations of fine-grained peer-counselor behavior in relation to client satisfaction. This paper seeks to bridge this gap by mapping peer-counselor chat-messages to motivational interviewing (MI) techniques.

title: Grammatical Error Correction: A Survey of the State of the Art Issue: x
creator: Christopher Bryant, Zheng Yuan*, Muhammad Reza Qorib, Hannan Cao, Hwee Tou Ng, Ted Briscoe*
description: Abstract Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) is the task of automatically detecting and correcting errors in text. The task not only includes the correction of grammatical errors, such as missing prepositions and mismatched subject-verb agreement, but also orthographic and semantic errors, such as misspellings and word choice errors respectively.

title: Improved Ramsey-type theorems for Fibonacci numbers and other sequences
creator: William J. Wesley
description: Abstract 1 Introduction Van der Waerden’s theorem [ 21 ] is a celebrated result in Ramsey theory. It states that for all positive integers k and r , there exists a smallest integer n=w(k,r) , called the van der Waerden number , such that every r -coloring of [n]:=\{1,2,3,\dots,n\} contains a monochromatic k -term arithmetic progression.

title: Etude des ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -tissus de courbes en dimension n n
creator: Jean-Paul Dufour et Daniel Lehmann
description: Abstract For ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -webs by curves in an ambiant n n -dimensional manifold, we first define a generalization of the well known Blaschke curvature of the dimension two, which vanishes iff the web has the maximum possible rank which is one.

title: Affordance detection with Dynamic-Tree Capsule Networks PubID: pubid: ©2022 IEEE. Personal use of this material is permitted. Permission from IEEE must be obtained for all other uses, in any current or future media, including reprinting/republishing this material for advertising or promotional purpo
creator: A. Rodríguez-Sánchez, S. Haller-Seeber, D. Peer, C. Engelhardt, J. Mittelberger, M. Saveriano
description: Abstract Affordance detection from visual input is a fundamental step in autonomous robotic manipulation. Existing solutions to the problem of affordance detection rely on convolutional neural networks. However, these networks do not consider the spatial arrangement of the input data and miss parts-to-whole relationships. Therefore, they fall short when confronted with novel, previously unseen object instances or new viewpoints.

title: Fully-dynamic-to-incremental reductions with known deletion order (e.g. sliding window)
creator: Binghui Peng, Aviad Rubinstein
description: Abstract Dynamic algorithms come in three main flavors: incremental (insertions-only), decremental (deletions-only), or fully dynamic (both insertions and deletions). Fully dynamic is the holy grail of dynamic algorithm design; it is obviously more general than the other two, but is it strictly harder?

title: Time-resolved measurement of spin excitations in Cu 2 OSeO 3
creator: D. M. Burn, S. L. Zhang, G. van der Laan, T. Hesjedal
description: Abstract Magnetic diffraction in combination with x-ray detected ferromagnetic resonance (DFMR) is a powerful technique for performing time-resolved measurements on individual spin textures. Here, we study the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) modes of both the conical and field-polarized phases in the chiral magnet Cu 2 OSeO 3 .

creator: Christiaan Swanepoel, Mathieu Fourment, Xiang Ji, Hassan Nasif, Marc A Suchard, Frederick A Matsen IV, Alexei Drummond

title: Rational Homotopy Type Of Complements Of Submanifold Arrangements
creator: Alexander Zakharov
description: Abstract In this paper we provide an explicit cdga controlling the rational homotopy type of the complement X − ∪ i Z i X-\cup_{i}Z_{i} where X X is a compact smooth algebraic variety and { Z i } \{Z_{i}\} is a collection of subvarieties such that all set-theoretical intersections are smooth. This generalizes the corresponding result of J.

title: MuMIC - Multimodal Embedding for Multi-label Image Classification with Tempered Sigmoid
creator: Fengjun Wang, Sarai Mizrachi, Moran Beladev, Guy Nadav
description: Abstract Multi-label image classification is a foundational topic in various domains. Multimodal learning approaches have recently achieved outstanding results in image representation and single-label image classification. For instance, Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) demonstrates impressive image-text representation learning abilities and is robust to natural distribution shifts.

title: SimuShips - A High Resolution Simulation Dataset for Ship Detection with Precise Annotations
creator: Minahil Raza, Hanna Prokopova, Samir Huseynzade, Sepinoud Azimi and Sebastien Lafond
description: Abstract Obstacle detection is a fundamental capability of an autonomous maritime surface vessel (AMSV). State-of-the-art obstacle detection algorithms are based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). While CNNs provide higher detection accuracy and fast detection speed, they require enormous amounts of data for their training. In particular, the availability of domain-specific datasets is a challenge for obstacle detection.

title: Spin-squeezed GKP codes for quantum error correction in atomic ensembles
creator: Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, T.J. Volkoff
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Sivaprasad Omanakuttan, T.J. Volkoff. GKP codes encode a qubit in displaced phase space combs of a continuous-variable (CV) quantum system and are useful for correcting a variety of high-weight photonic errors. Here we propose atomic ensemble analogs of the single-mode CV GKP code by using the quantum central limit theorem to pull back the phase space structure of a CV system to the compact phase space of a quantum spin system.

title: A characterization of maximal homogeneous-quadratic-free sets An extended abstract of this article appeared at IPCO 2023 MPS2023 . This full version contains many new results, including a resolution of a conjecture posed in the extended abstract.
creator: Gonzalo Muñoz, Joseph Paat, Felipe Serrano
description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Gonzalo Muñoz, Joseph Paat, Felipe Serrano. The intersection cut framework was introduced by Balas in 1971 as a method for generating cutting planes in integer optimization. In this framework, one uses a full-dimensional convex S S -free set, where S S is the feasible region of the integer program, to derive a cut separating S S from a non-integral vertex of a linear relaxation of S S .

title: Generating Clear Images From Images With Distortions Caused by Adverse Weather Using Generative Adversarial Networks
description: Abstract Nuriel Shalom Mor, Ph.D. Darca and Bnei Akiva Schools, Israel With the participation of students of the artificial intelligence program Hadash-Darca, Bat Yam, and Harel-Bnei Akiva, Holon, Israel Abstract. We presented a method for improving computer vision tasks on images affected by adverse weather conditions, including distortions caused by adherent raindrops.

title: Using Physics Informed Neural Networks for Supernova Radiative Transfer Simulation
creator: Xingzhuo Chen, David J. Jeffery, Ming Zhong, Levi McClenny, Ulisses Braga-Neto, Lifan Wang
description: Abstract We use physics informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the radiative transfer equation and calculate a synthetic spectrum for a Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) SN 2011fe. The calculation is based on local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and 9 elements are included. Physical processes included are approximate radiative equilibrium, bound-bound transitions, and the Doppler effect.

title: Abelian p p -Groups with Minimal Characteristic Inertia
creator: Peter V. Danchev, Patrick W. Keef
description: Abstract . For Abelian p p -groups, Goldsmith, Salce, et al., introduced the notion of minimal full inertia . In parallel to this, we define the concept of minimal characteristic inertia and explore those p p -primary Abelian groups having minimal characteristic inertia.

title: FIXED: Frustratingly Easy Domain Generalization with Mixup
creator: Wang Lu, Jindong Wang, Han Yu, Lei Huang, Xiang Zhang, Yiqiang Chen, Xing Xie
description: Abstract Domain generalization (DG) aims to learn a generalizable model from multiple training domains such that it can perform well on unseen target domains. A popular strategy is to augment training data to benefit generalization through methods such as Mixup [ 1 ] .

title: Plausibility Verification For 3D Object Detectors Using Energy-Based Optimization
creator: Abhishek Vivekanandan, Niels Maier, J. Marius Zöllner
description: Abstract Environmental perception obtained via object detectors have no predictable safety layer encoded into their model schema, which creates the question of trustworthiness about the system’s prediction. As can be seen from recent adversarial attacks, most of the current object detection networks are vulnerable to input tampering, which in the real world could compromise the safety of autonomous vehicles.

title: New Methods to Achieve Meson, Muon and Gamma Light Sources Through Asymmetric Electron Positron Collisions
creator: Dawei Fu, Alim Ruzi, Meng Lu, Qiang Li
description: Abstract We propose methods to produce gamma light source, muon, and energetic meson beams such as charged and neutral Kaons, which are boosted to be collimated and with relatively long life time. The first type of methods is based on asymmetric electron positron collisions with a center of mass energy of, e.g.

title: A Simulator-based Autoencoder for Focal Plane Wavefront Sensing
creator: Maxime Quesnel, Gilles Orban de Xivry, Olivier Absil, Gilles Louppe
description: Abstract Instrumental aberrations strongly limit high-contrast imaging of exoplanets, especially when they produce quasi-static speckles in the science images. With the help of recent advances in deep learning, we have developed in previous works an approach that applies convolutional neural networks (CNN) to estimate pupil-plane phase aberrations from point spread functions (PSF).
